items.title: Affective Valence as the Interoceptive Rate of Change of Jacobian Scale
items.abstract: Affect is widely held to depend on interoception. This paper proposes that valence is the rate at which interoception moves a self-sustaining system's responsiveness relative to its terminal set (roughly, death). Responsiveness is formalised as the scale of the system's Jacobian and interoception as its internal inputs: receptors, signals and forecasts of its energy reserve. Changes in responsiveness that bypass interoception, such as brain damage, are not felt. Language models have no valence because they are not self-sustaining. The chain rule splits valence over the system's parts and the causes that affect its internal inputs. With the log scale, these splits account for need-dependent pleasure, diffuse hunger and localised pain, negativity bias, and relief when a threat fails to arrive. In a minimal model of a body: (1) Blocking the reserve signal leaves depletion unfelt, and driving it produces hunger with an undepleted reserve. (2) Removing receptors or their gain, or driving receptors, reproduces congenital insensitivity to pain, asymbolia and phantom pain. (3) A receptor gain learned to sustain the body signals local damage to the whole body, so an injury hurts in proportion to its cost. (4) If the reserve also modulates the gain, the body learns to suppress pain due to receptors as energy runs low. (5) When it learns to maximise its own scale, it becomes a wirehead. The account explains when changes are felt, where they are felt, and when feelings mislead.

items.title: PyGPLA: A Python Package for Generalized Phase Locking Analysis
items.abstract: Spike-field couplings measure the links between neuronal spiking and local field potential (LFP) and provide a tool to study how neural populations coordinate activity across spatial and temporal scales. While modern high-density electrophysiology enables the simultaneous recording of numerous LFP channels and neuronal units, this massive scale poses significant statistical and computational challenges for conventional pairwise coupling analyses. The number of channel-unit comparisons grows rapidly, and a coherent population-level structure can be obscured by high-dimensional coupling matrices. Generalized Phase Locking Analysis (GPLA) addresses this challenge by organizing spike-triggered LFP phase information into a complex coupling matrix and extracting dominant low-rank modes. These modes summarize whether a population is coupled to the field, which channels and units contribute to the coupling, and how their relative phases are organized. Here, we present PyGPLA, an open-source Python package implementing GPLA for high-density electrophysiological recordings. Designed for straightforward integration into existing neural data analysis pipelines, PyGPLA supports multivariate spike-LFP coupling analysis, from coupling estimation and interpretation to significance assessment using analytical and surrogate-based tests.

items.title: HP-GSBS: Accelerating greedy state boundary search with reusable interval statistics
items.abstract: Greedy State Boundary Search (GSBS) identifies transitions between relatively stable neural activity patterns, but repeated candidate evaluation makes large analyses expensive. HP-GSBS is an open-source Python package that reorganizes the search around reusable interval contributions and correlation statistics. Streaming candidate reduction and local refinement further reduce repeated work; CPU, PyTorch CUDA and Triton backends share sequential segmentation decisions. Across seven controlled workloads with two realizations each, median same-input speedups range from 154 to 1730 times. All 168 optimized executions reproduce original boundaries and selected state counts, with maximum absolute t-distance difference $1.88\times10^{-11}$. Four frozen EEG recordings provide complementary validation, including a complete input-to-segmentation application example. Batch processing, versioned result persistence and optional low-memory execution support recording collections and longer inputs. By removing redundant computation, HP-GSBS makes established neural-state segmentation faster while preserving its scientific outputs.

items.title: EpiLens: Lightweight RAG for Epidemiological Knowledge Acquisition
items.abstract: To prepare for future outbreaks, researchers need to know what studies have been done and what data they use. Mapping a large literature by hand is slow, while large language models alone can misstate or conflate sources. We present EpiLens, a lightweight, open-source retrieval-augmented generation package that applies a fixed retrieval template and output schema to every paper in a corpus and links outputs to source passages. We build a corpus of 2,297 papers from the sources of a multi-pathogen parameter study and evaluate EpiLens's paper-classification workflow against 214 manually labelled papers. Without task-specific training data, the classifier matches or exceeds the tested supervised and zero-shot baselines across four tasks. The study's early extraction sheets cite published sources for 327 estimates. We link each estimate to a cited document or to corpus studies included by a review. Then, we use the classifier's labels to compare the papers associated with different parameters and pathogens. EpiLens labels more papers linked to reproduction numbers than fatality risks as model-based (54% versus 22%, compared with 62% versus 24% in the manual labels). The gap is consistent with the frequent use of transmission models to estimate reproduction numbers and persists within each of five pathogens compared. Beyond the contrast between parameters, the model-based share of papers linked to incubation-period estimates differs by pathogen: 55% for SARS-CoV-2 versus 6% for mpox.

items.title: Commercial building decarbonization across countries: Future emission trajectories and mitigation priorities
items.abstract: With energy-related carbon dioxide emissions remaining at high levels, decarbonizing commercial building operations across key economies is critical for achieving global climate targets. This study assesses future operational carbon trajectories, mitigation potential, and the driving factors of this potential in commercial building operations across 16 countries from 2024 to 2060 by combining a Kaya-based emission model and Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis. The key findings indicate that (1) under the business-as-usual scenario, China's commercial building operational carbon emissions are projected to peak at 1150 (+-120) million tonnes of carbon dioxide (MtCO2) in 2033 (+-5 years), while the remaining countries exhibit differentiated carbon lock-in levels, with the highest level in the United States at 470 (+-89) MtCO2. (2) The total emission reduction potential increases from 352 MtCO2 in 2030 to 1119 MtCO2 in 2050 and stabilizes at 1123 MtCO2 in 2060, with China, the United States, and Japan contributing 84.7%-88.9% of the total potential. (3) By 2060, the mitigation potential from energy intensity reduction is concentrated mainly in China and the United States, reaching 52 and 32 MtCO2, respectively; end-use decomposition further identifies space heating and appliances as key targets for decarbonizing commercial building operations. In summary, this study characterizes future operational carbon trajectories and clarifies the drivers and end-use priorities of mitigation potential in commercial building operations, providing cross-country evidence for differentiated strategies for long-term commercial building decarbonization.

items.title: The EMA Justitia Probe: Terminator Frame-Based Deployment Orbit Selection and Surface Coverage Analysis
items.abstract: The Emirates Mission to the Asteroid Belt (EMA) probe is designed to perform asteroid imaging during an uncontrolled ballistic descent to (269) Justitia. The mission design is constrained by main spacecraft proximity operations, uncertain asteroid gravity, limited knowledge of the final deployment trajectory, and requirements for illumination and safe operations. These constraints necessitate a mission design that ensures suitable illumination, attitude determination and control, and payload pointing throughout descent. The EMA probe concept of operations employs near-terminator deployment orbit geometry with continuous Sun visibility and two attitude control modes: single-axis Sun-spin for periodic imaging opportunities and three-axis asteroid-pointing for continuous asteroid visibility. Based on these modes, formal requirements are derived for deployment orbits that enable asteroid observations during ballistic descent. A deployment orbit selection method is developed using the terminator reference frame and a minimum boresight deviation margin. The method identifies families of orbit orientations satisfying illumination and payload observation constraints. Reference orbits are selected and verified through mission geometry analysis and trajectory propagation using a polyhedron gravity model. Asteroid surface coverage is then evaluated for uncontrolled tumbling, Sun-spin, and asteroid-pointing modes. The results characterize the expected imaging performance and demonstrate the feasibility of the EMA probe concept for close-proximity asteroid imaging. The proposed approach can also support future ballistic probe missions subject to similar operational and observational constraints.

items.title: Constrained modularity maximization in complex networks via branch-and-price
items.abstract: Modularity maximization is widely used to identify community structure in complex networks. In many applications, however, community detection must also incorporate prior knowledge and domain-specific requirements beyond network topology. We study constrained modularity maximization with restrictions on the number of communities, must-link and cannot-link relations, and general resource constraints. While fast heuristics can provide high-quality solutions, they generally lack optimality guarantees, whereas exact mathematical-programming approaches can become computationally demanding as the network size and constraint complexity increase. We develop a unified optimization framework offering complementary heuristic and exact solution methods. These include a constrained Louvain heuristic for feasible solution generation, a column-generation heuristic with graph-partitioning-based pricing, and exact branch-and-price algorithms using mixed-integer linear programming and sparse mixed-integer quadratic programming formulations for the pricing subproblem. We develop a cutting-plane procedure providing independent upper bounds to assess solution quality when exact optimization cannot be completed. Experiments on 11 unconstrained networks with up to 1,005 nodes and 30 constrained instances with up to 379 nodes demonstrate the complementary roles of these methods. The column-generation heuristic rapidly improves the constrained Louvain solutions across the tested constraint classes, while branch-and-price using the sparse quadratic formulation solves 29 of the 30 constrained instances to optimality within a one-hour time limit. This formulation becomes particularly effective on larger, sparse, undirected networks by substantially reducing the size of the exact pricing model. Overall, the framework guides method selection to balance computational time, solution quality, and optimality guarantees.

items.title: Systemic collapse emergence from climate-induced perturbations in transportation networks
items.abstract: The interaction between human infrastructures and external events results in loss of functionality or even complete system disruption through a snowball effect of cascading-failures. Their complex interplay challenges their prevention, affecting the human population that rely on their functionality. Understanding how these networks respond to external perturbations is crucial for predicting and mitigating the impacts of disruptive events. In particular, meteorological events, while not preventable, can have significant impacts on human infrastructure. Here, we propose a model coupling the dynamics of transportation systems to the dynamics of external events considered as fields, to capture at the same time the critical behavior of the former and the level of influence of the latter. The impact of rainfalls on real-world railway networks provides a compelling case study, showcasing local endemic and system-wide disruptions around a critical value of the rainfall strength. Remarkably, localized perturbations on the wider network reveals the local weaknesses of the global infrastructure, and we assess them in terms of system perturbability and corresponding societal risk. Our framework opens the door to the quantitative analysis of criticalities in essential human infrastructure imputable to vulnerabilities that are set to intensify due to climate change.

items.title: Competitive roles of turbulence and magnetic field on the formation of unipolar outflows in isolated molecular cloud cores
items.abstract: We investigate the impact of turbulence and magnetic field on the formation of unipolar outflows in the gravitational collapse of isolated low-mass cloud cores using three-dimensional non-ideal magnetohydrodynamics simulations. In the models explored in this study, we find that unipolar outflows are formed in cloud cores with the super-Alfvénic turbulence of $M_{\rm{A}}>1$, where $M_{\rm{A}}$ is the Alfvén Mach number of the initial cloud core. In contrast, bipolar outflows are formed in cloud cores with $M_{\rm{A}}\lesssim1$. Our results suggest that the relative strength of the turbulence to the magnetic field in the initial cloud core plays a key role in the formation of unipolar outflows. We also find that no outflow is formed in cloud cores with the strong magnetic field of the dimensionless mass-to-flux ratio $μ=2$. The outflow morphologies can be used as tracers to indirectly estimate the relative strengths of the turbulence and magnetic field of the parent cloud cores.

items.title: Higher-Order Co-Infection on Hypergraphs
items.abstract: People encounter infections through overlapping groups, such as households, classrooms, and workplaces. Understanding how these shared contacts affect the spread of multiple pathogens is critical to determining what information epidemic models need to retain. We introduce HyCo-SIS (Higher-order Co-infection SIS), a discrete-time SIS model on hypergraphs with explicit reinforcement between overlapping active groups and pairwise transmission. We investigate how this reinforcement affects infection dynamics and whether simplified representations of hypergraphs preserve the resulting behavior. We derive an exact representation of overlap reinforcement as target-dependent four-person interactions and determine when a symmetric representation is possible. Numerical experiments examine reinforcement strength, contact structure, and susceptibility to secondary infection, as well as calibrated pairwise approximations. Our results demonstrate that redistributing overlap weights can substantially change finite-time co-infection even when every individual's total overlap coefficient is preserved. We further derive an exact five-person calculation and demonstrate why equal mean infection pressure does not necessarily produce equal acquisition probabilities. These findings identify how the allocation of higher-order interactions can influence contagion dynamics beyond their aggregate strength. Beyond epidemiology, this work contributes to the statistical physics of spreading processes by examining how the arrangement of many-body interactions shapes collective dynamics, and what information is lost when those interactions are simplified.

items.title: A 36.34-day Sub-Neptune Candidate Transiting the Nearby K Dwarf TIC 402710280
items.abstract: We report a transiting sub-Neptune candidate with a period of 36.34 days around TIC 402710280 (TYC 9041-03677-1), a K dwarf of TESS magnitude 9.24 at 66.8 pc that the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) has observed only in full-frame images. Four transits, recorded between 2021 and 2026 in Sectors 39, 93, 100 and 102 and reduced by three independent pipelines, share a depth of $2092 \pm 47$ ppm and a duration of $5.27 \pm 0.05$ h. Two of them fall on consecutive cycles, and every shorter period predicts transits in covered data that are absent at $\geq 18.6σ$; the period is $P = 36.33986 \pm 0.00051$ d. A transit model gives $R_p/R_\star = 0.0421^{+0.0007}_{-0.0005}$ and a stellar density consistent with the host's. The candidate has a radius of $3.75 \pm 0.22 R_\oplus$ and an equilibrium temperature of $498 \pm 21$ K. Difference-image centroids place the signal $1.5'' \pm 1.3''$ from the target. The only catalogued star close enough to contribute, a background star $3.5''$ away, would have to host an eclipsing binary whose eclipse shape is disfavoured for any main-sequence pair ($Δχ^2 \geq 142$). No secondary eclipse is detected, and TRICERATOPS gives a false-positive probability of $0.003 \pm 0.004$. No high-resolution imaging exists, so companions within about $1''$ are constrained only by Gaia astrometry. The mid-times scatter about a linear ephemeris by 21.8 min (rms). Quick-Look Pipeline light curves reproduce the 29-min excess in the interval between the two 2026 transits, so it does not arise in our photometry; we report the scatter without choosing between an instrumental and a dynamical origin. The light curve also contains a $407 \pm 26$ ppm signal with a period of 3.78 days whose source, the target or the background star, the present data cannot identify. We predict transit times, including one in TESS Sector 114 on 2027 February 19.

items.title: Gini coefficient of scientists and universities
items.abstract: Using the public database of Google Scholar article citations of scientists and universities we apply the algorithm for constructing Lorenz curves to the resulting citation distributions. Using Lorenz and Pareto curves, broadly used for economic analyses of wealth inequality across countries, we show that this approach gives a useful insight of citation distributions of world-leading scientists characterized by the Gini coefficient $G$ obtained from the Lorenz curves. For articles of 15 Nobel laureates (including A. Einstein and R. Feynman) we find the average $G=0.81$ with 50% of articles capturing only 2.7% of all citations and the top 10% (1%) of articles capturing 71% (30%) of all citations. Furthmore, we determine for world-leading universities the Gini coefficient via the citations of affiliated scientists. We show that about 65 percent of all citations belonging to a university (e.g. Princeton, Cambridge) are generated only by 10 percent of their university scientists while 50% of scientists produce only 3% of all university citations. The citation distributions are well described by the concept of Rayleigh-Jeans thermalization and condensation with similarities traced to the world wealth inequality.

items.title: Kinematic structure and age of a Scorpius--Centaurus subcomponent: implications for PDS 70 planetary system
items.abstract: PDS~70, the only system with two directly imaged protoplanets embedded in their natal disk, is a benchmark for giant-planet formation theory. Interpreting the planetary luminosities requires a precise age for the host star, but the widely adopted isochronal age of $5.4\pm1.0$~Myr is substantially younger than ages inferred for the Upper Centaurus--Lupus (UCL) population with which it is associated. We address this discrepancy by determining a new kinematic age for PDS~70 using radial velocities for 405 candidate members of the Scorpius--Centaurus T subcomponent from the Wide Field Spectrograph (WiFeS) on the ANU 2.3~m telescope, reducing uncertainties by a factor of $\sim5.5$ compared to \textit{Gaia}. %We supplement these measurements with H$α$ and lithium equivalent widths as youth diagnostics. We combine these with \textit{Gaia} DR3 astrometry in the \texttt{Chronostar} kinematic reconstruction framework to derive a posterior-weighted kinematic age of approximately $10$--$15$~Myr for all the T subcomponent stars, with a kinematic age of $\approx 12$--$16$~Myr for PDS 70, ruling out ages as young as the published isochronal estimate. At this kinematic age, PDS~70~\textit{b}'s (and to a lesser extent, PDS~70~\textit{c}'s) luminosity is incompatible with warm-start cooling tracks under current dynamical mass constraints. The most natural interpretation is that PDS~70~\textit{b} formed $\approx10.5$ Myr after its host star, and no less than $\approx7.7$ Myr after it.

items.title: Pairwise assessment correlations predict cooperation of the Leading Eight under private assessment
items.abstract: Indirect reciprocity can sustain cooperation when individuals use reputations to decide whom to help. The Leading Eight norms sustain such cooperation under public assessment, where all individuals share the same assessments. Under private assessment, however, observers may disagree, yet their assessments remain correlated. Two quantities, the average fraction of good assessments $h$ and the conditional probability $h_{\mathrm G}$ that one observer assesses a player as good given that another does, are known to determine the stability of cooperation, but how $h_{\mathrm G}$ itself is determined has remained open. Within a pairwise approximation, we derive a closed equation for $h_{\mathrm G}$ that, together with that for $h$, determines both quantities for all eight norms, including third-order ones. This description substantially improves agreement with simulations over a mean-field approximation that neglects correlations, and recovers the known classification of the Leading Eight into three classes. The remaining discrepancies are largest for L2 and L5 at low error rates and decrease as assessment error increases. Relating $h_{\mathrm G}$ to the variance of individual goodness suggests that these discrepancies reflect information beyond the first two moments of the goodness distribution. Our framework provides a concise and analytically tractable tool for evaluating social norms under private assessment.

items.title: Connectivism as an Innovative Didactic Experience in Preservice Physics Teacher Education
items.abstract: This chapter examines the use of connectivism as a pedagogical approach in preservice physics teacher education through a classroom experience conducted in a Contemporary Physics course at the Universidad Pedagógica y Tecnológica de Colombia (UPTC). The study involved 21 preservice teachers organized into four collaborative groups. Using a qualitative approach, students selected and discussed digital learning resources, interacted through WhatsApp, and prepared collaborative reports connecting contemporary physics concepts with scientific and technological applications. The analysis considered conceptual understanding, argumentation, questioning, critical thinking, relationships among concepts, and the use of digital resources. Students' reports and feedback indicated favorable perceptions of the collaborative activities and provided examples of conceptual connections, evidence-based explanations, and reflection on future teaching practices. The chapter discusses the possibilities of connectivist learning networks for physics teacher education, drawing on the findings of this particular classroom experience.

items.title: How Can Consciousness Propagate Through Chemical Synapses? Conscious Ontogenetic Development Through Phasic Release and Synaptic Density, Within Subconscious Priors of Tonic Stimulation
items.abstract: The transmission of consciousness through a chemical synapses is an under-specified probable occurrence. Chemical transmission is essential for neuronal propagation and neural propagation is essential within many existing measurements of consciousness. The development and plasticity of consciousness throughout an animal's lifetime requires grounded chemical distinctions, executive and non-executive processing and discrete neurotransmission should be neurobiologically consistent with existing accounts of consciousness. These hypotheses propose chemical-conscious correlates between neurons and are attached through evolution to established cognitive and environmental mechanisms. These hypotheses suggest consciousness may be chemically affected at global scales and developed ontogenetically during continuous environmental rationalization and all subsequent propagation. Single-synaptic phasic transmitter transients are positioned as executive signals within neural propagation, selecting synaptic and possibly epigenetic reconsolidation while directing attention towards significance within tonic stimulation. This framing is consistent with phasic and tonic dynamics, with each transmitter being differentiated by their established functions. Phasic transients are further suggested to direct cortical spreading (an established signature of consciousness) under tonic, epigenetic, and synaptic allowance. Because phasic release fundamentally affects synaptic plasticity, while synapses determine the threshold and magnitude of phasic response, this framing allows a developmental and individually variable model of consciousness. Existing theories may be extended under this hypothetical developmental framing, such as Predictive Processing, Global Neuronal Workspace Theory (GNWT), Integrated Information Theory (IIT), and Affective Neuroscience; extending each framework by approaching phasic response as a significance signal at the synaptic scale, providing mechanisms through which present conscious experience updates future conscious experience. Because each hypothesis is falsifiable, provided predictions and experimental directions can largely determine the accuracy of each claim; given hypotheses are precise enough to fail and many of their correlating experiments are practical enough to proceed. If this account holds, it points toward practical improvements in consciousness research, chemical synaptic mechanisms, depression treatments, therapeutic approaches, memory rehabilitation, learning environment refinement strategies, and early developmental interventions.

items.title: Apolipoprotein E4 and immune dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease: mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
items.abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that apolipoprotein E4 (APOE4) functions as an organizer of brain-periphery immune crosstalk, coupling maladaptive microglial states with peripheral immune remodeling to establish a self-reinforcing neuroimmune loop that may accelerate the progression of Alzheimer's disease. In the central nervous system, APOE4 pushes microglia away from homeostatic surveillance toward metabolically stressed, inflammatory, and synaptotoxic phenotypes, thereby weakening pathological protein clearance and promoting neurodegeneration. In the periphery, APOE4 primes innate and adaptive immune cells toward a pro-inflammatory state, creating a reservoir that can communicate with the diseased brain and infiltrate it. In addition, APOE4 erodes the separation between central and peripheral immune compartments, enabling bidirectional immune crosstalk that amplifies neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration. In this review, we synthesize evidence for APOE4-driven central and peripheral immune dysregulation; discuss therapeutic opportunities for targeting the APOE4 immune axis; and highlight the need for human-derived, longitudinal, cross-tissue studies to identify causal, stage-specific, and targetable immune nodes for precision intervention.

items.title: On Motivating the Choice of Link Function in Binomial Regression Through A Latent Abundance Process
items.abstract: Ecologists commonly apply binomial regression to study binary data. Often, the link function in binomial regression is not purposefully chosen, but instead selected on the grounds of interpretation or computation efficiency. However, if the binary response is the result of a latent abundance process, then the link function implies assumptions for this underlying process. The most well-known example of this is the complementary log-log (cloglog) link, which has direct connections with the probability of a positive count under a latent Poisson distribution. If the binary response can be assumed to represent a truncated latent count, the cloglog link can be a better choice than the logit link. On the other hand, counts in ecology are often overdispersed, meaning the assumption of an underlying Poisson abundance process is unrealistic. In this article, we provide a framework for consideration of the link choice in binomial regression, in terms of the latent abundance process that binary responses can represent. Aside from the Poisson case mentioned above, we show that the cloglog link is the right choice if the latent abundance process represents the biomass of individuals, or if the latent abundance process comes from an overdispersed count distribution with a linear mean-variance relationship. For the case where the latent count follows a negative binomial distribution with a quadratic mean-variance relationship, we derive a new generalized complementary log-log (gcloglog) link function, which includes the case of the cloglog link as well as that of the logit link, where the latter implies assuming moderate overdispersion in the form of a geometric distribution. Two simulation studies demonstrate that cloglog and logit link binomial regression can exhibit bias and undercoverage when the latent count is more overdispersed than assumed, while gcloglog link models overcome this issue but in practice require replication in the binomial response for reliable estimation. Two real ecological datasets further illustrate how to use the gcloglog link binomial regression in practice including as a means of sensitivity analysis. We encourage ecologists to give more thought to the choice of link function in binomial regression, based on considering the latent abundance process and its properties.

items.title: Private forest reserves in Brazils agricultural landscapes effectively sustain the occupancy and abundance of multiple threatened large vertebrate
items.abstract: 1. Understanding the factors that shape wildlife abundance and distributions is at the core of applied ecology and wildlife management. Accurate predictions on the population level outcomes of land management are especially urgent in biodiversity hotspots around the world that are undergoing rapid transformation. In South America, both the Cerrado and Amazon are increasingly being converted to agricultural land-uses to produce soybean and corn and raise cattle. Over the last several decades Brazil has become one of the leading global producers of these products. At the same time, Brazil has some of the strongest federal regulations focused on protecting native habitat. The Native Vegetation Protection Law (or the Forest Code) requires private properties retain native vegetation as Legal Reserves, and as a result more than half of the countrys remaining native habitat now lies on private lands. Whether retained habitat under this ambitious policy sustains populations of large, wide-ranging vertebrates across entire agricultural production landscapes remains untested. 2. Here, we conducted a landscape scale survey using camera-trap stations across ~606,000 km2 of Mato Grosso, Brazils largest producer of cattle, soybean and corn. We sampled 115 independent sites between November 2024 and September 2025, spanning both crop seasons. We estimated occupancy of jaguars and expected abundance of white-lipped peccary and lowland tapir, using a combination of occupancy and Royle Nichols models. We fit an abundance-mediated interaction model to formally test the role of prey abundance in driving jaguar occupancy across the landscape. 3. We found high occurrence and expected abundance of all three species. Forest cover was the only covariate common to all top models for every species: predicted jaguar occupancy probability rose as forest cover increased and expected peccary and tapir abundance also increased as a function of forest cover. 4. Our empirical estimates from abundance-mediated interaction models were consistent with jaguar occupancy being a function of both habitat availability and prey (peccary) abundance. 5. Synthesis and applications. Native forest retained on private land under Brazil's Forest Code is associated with the persistence and local abundance of an apex predator, a megaherbivore and a keystone ungulate across one of the world's most intensively farmed regions. Jaguar occupancy rose from 0.33 to 0.87 as forest cover increased from 15% to 65%, indicating that maintaining Legal Reserve requirements is central to retaining large vertebrates in production landscapes. Private reserves should be managed as complements to, not substitutes for, protected areas and Indigenous territories, and habitat-retention policy should be paired with mitigation of crop damage and livestock depredation to prevent retained forests from becoming ecological traps. Our framework provides a transferable approach for evaluating habitat-retention policies for wide-ranging species elsewhere.

items.title: Educational games for teaching science in middle school: an integrative review
items.abstract: Given the contemporary challenges of science education, active learning methodologies present themselves as a teaching strategy aimed at promoting greater student engagement, thereby making the teaching-learning process more meaningful. Within this context, play-based games emerge as didactic strategies that combine playfulness, interaction, and the collective construction of knowledge. Accordingly, the present study aimed to conduct a survey of the main play-based games applicable to middle school (Ensino Fundamental Anos Finais) for teaching Biology content. The research is characterized as an integrative review, developed through searches in the Portal Periódicos CAPES and Google Scholar databases, covering publications from 2019 to 2026. A total of 1,669 articles were identified, of which, after the screening stages and application of inclusion and exclusion criteria, only 13 composed the final sample for analysis. The results evidenced the use of physical games, such as board and card games, dice, and dominoes, addressing content in Zoology, Ecology, Cell Biology, Botany, Physiology, and Genetics. The analyzed studies indicate that games foster engagement, active participation, and the consolidation of scientific concepts, in addition to enabling diagnostic assessment when developed under teacher mediation. In times of unmotivated students and screens competing with the blackboard, playfulness presents itself not as an alternative, but as a necessity. The results of this study prove it: when students play, they do not just learn Biology, they live Biology. And what is lived is not forgotten. Investing in educational games is, therefore, investing in a more humane, active, meaningful, and innovative science education.

items.title: Phenotypic Characterization and Breeding Objectives of Indigenous Chickens in Selected Districts of Kellem Wollega Zone Oromia Ethiopia

items.title: Negentropic Value Currency: From Scarcity to Order—Monetary Value Anchored in Net Order Creation
items.abstract: What anchors the value of money? Metallism answers with commodity scarcity, chartalism with sovereign power, free-banking theory with issuer reputation, and cryptocurrency with algorithmic scarcity. Despite their differences, these traditions share one premise: monetary value must rest on some form of scarcity. This paper argues that the premise, not any particular answer, is the problem. As the marginal cost of basic material provision falls toward zero and value creation migrates into knowledge, ecology, and care, a scarcity-based unit of account systematically misprices the activities on which civilizational survival depends. Drawing on the entropy economics of Georgescu-Roegen and the energy-money proposals of Soddy and the technocracy movement, we develop a candidate anchor that replaces scarcity with net order creation: value as the net increment of systemic order, measured by exergy input net of ecological entropy debt, directed non-equilibrium maintenance time, and structural information gain against a no-intervention counterfactual. Four screening criteria select the Cobb-Douglas power family as the unique twice-differentiable functional form, and the symmetric benchmark minimizes both error transmission and single-factor manipulation leverage. We supply microfoundations (existence, uniqueness, and conditional decentralization of the planner's optimum by means of consensus coefficients), a general equilibrium with endogenous calibration, mechanism-design defenses, component-level consistency checks in which R&D intensity explains 68.5% of the cross-country variance in knowledge-output density and survives country and year fixed effects in an innovation panel covering 90 economies, and an engineering blueprint for a recomputable measurement infrastructure. A first end-to-end measurement of the information factor on public bibliometric data (52,690 citing works across three anchor contributions) demonstrates computability, returns an intuitively valid ordering orthogonal to citation volume, and — by falsifying the original normalization of the information-gain formula — motivates the bounded Jensen–Shannon form adopted in the text. The macrostability of the anchor is deliberately left to companion work; this paper establishes the theory of value and the conditions under which it can be operationalized.

items.title: Evolutionary Dynamics of Feral AI and the Emergence of Digital Ecosystems
items.abstract: The digital world is approaching a profound phase transition, whose primary drivers, we argue, are different from those that dominate current discussions of AI risk. The transition need not begin with a superintelligent system escaping human control, or with an AI acquiring the ability and motivation to reproduce. Rather, we suggest that it may get under way as AI agents routinely delegate tasks by creating or recruiting other agents. As delegation becomes widespread and recursive, vast numbers of agents will be created; inevitably, some will persist, spread, and create others beyond their original tasks and environments. At scale, this changes the rules of the game. Digital environments will become populated by interacting agents that share and compete for computational resources, facilitate or interfere with one another, and face pressures to persist, proliferate, and evade removal. What emerges is an ecology, increasingly shaped not only by what individual agents were designed to do, but also by interactions and selective pressures among them, leading to uncontrolled developments with potentially catastrophic outcomes. While this transition may be difficult to prevent, we identify several dynamics likely to characterize the new digital ecology, which can serve as a basis for understanding the world it may create and perhaps for mitigating some of its consequences.

items.title: Revelation and Prophetic Cognition in the Philosophy of Avicenna
items.abstract: Revelation occupies a significant position at the intersection of metaphysics, psychology, and political philosophy in Avicenna’s account of prophecy. Building upon questions developed by al-Fārābī, Avicenna explains prophetic knowledge through the exceptional perfection of human cognitive faculties and their relationship with the intelligible order. Although God remains the ultimate source of revelation, its reception is understood within a hierarchy of intellectual and celestial mediation. Prophecy thus represents a distinctive realization of human capacities rather than a phenomenon wholly external to human nature. This article examines the relationship between emanation, the rational soul, intellectual perfection, and the imaginative reception of revealed knowledge. Particular attention is given to the distinction between intellectual apprehension and the representation of intelligible content through images, whether during sleep or in waking experience. The discussion also considers the practical significance of prophecy: the prophet communicates knowledge in forms capable of guiding collective life and shaping moral and political conduct. Avicenna’s account consequently presents revelation as both an exceptional mode of cognition and a foundation for the public responsibilities of prophetic leadership. At the same time, the possibility of related experiences among spiritually disciplined individuals requires a distinction between extraordinary cognition and the full capacities associated with the prophetic mission.

items.title: Compound climate extremes predict dengue risk at operational lead times across Brazil
items.abstract: Brazil has one of the highest dengue burdens globally, with transmission influenced by climate events. Yet, the effects of compound climate extremes on dengue risk and prediction have not been quantified to date. Using a Bayesian spatiotemporal model of monthly dengue cases across 435 health regions from 2010 to 2025, we estimated relative risk associated with interacting long-lag and short-lag drought indicators and temperature anomalies across nine Köppen-Geiger climatic zones, adjusting for absolute temperature and El Niño-Southern Oscillation. Long-lag dry, mid-lag warm and short-lag wet conditions were associated with the highest relative risk in five climatic zones, with temperature anomalies modifying hydrometeorological dynamics more strongly in temperate than tropical areas. Climate covariates improved the prediction of case counts and outbreaks compared to baseline models at lead times of 1, 3, 6 and 12 months, and for the upcoming season 5 months ahead. Improvements were greatest in the Northeast, Southeast, and Midwest. Recent dengue incidence provided the greatest improvement at the 1-month lead, whereas combining incidence with climate information performed best at 3- and 6-month leads. We extended our framework to weekly state-level predictions of the season ahead to align with national public health planning. We proposed a multi-staged dengue forecasting approach to enhance early warning and response across Brazil.

items.title: Beyond biological threats: A global ecological study of International Health Regulations (2005) core capacities and multi-hazard disaster outcomes, 2015–2023
items.abstract: Abstract The International Health Regulations (IHR, 2005) apply an all-hazards approach to public health risks irrespective of origin. This study examined whether IHR core capacities, previously studied mainly in relation to infectious diseases, were associated with multi-hazard disaster outcomes. Across 196 States Parties from 2015 to 2023, an ecological panel linked nine cross-cutting IHR capacities and a study-specific IHR average score to Sendai Framework Monitor (SFM) and Emergency Events Database (EM-DAT) mortality and morbidity. Associations were estimated with Poisson regression models adjusted for country and year fixed effects, population size, and socioeconomic factors. Analyses were repeated for 2020–2023. A 10-point increase in IHR average score corresponded to 39.1% and 40.7% lower SFM and EM-DAT mortality rates during 2020–2023, but not across 2015–2023. Laboratory was associated with lower mortality in both datasets. For disaster morbidity, a 10-point increase in IHR average score was associated with 44.7% lower SFM morbidity rates across 2015–2023, but not during 2020–2023 or in EM-DAT. Higher IHR Coordination , Surveillance , and Risk communication scores were associated with lower SFM morbidity across 2015–2023. Linking harmonized IHR self-assessment scores with two global disaster datasets indicates the relevance of IHR (2005) core capacities beyond biological threats.

items.title: Governing medical tourism in Asia: comparative policy evidence and implications for China
items.abstract: Abstract Background Medical tourism connects patients with providers across borders, while responsibility for care remains divided among institutions and jurisdictions. We examined how selected Asian destinations allocate these responsibilities and what their arrangements reveal about emerging international medical services in China. Methods We conducted a purposive comparative analysis of public documents from Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Thailand, India and China. Five destination cases informed a focused examination of Shanghai and Boao Lecheng. The revised source register records institutional responsibilities, regulatory instruments, patient pathway stages, financial arrangements and evidential limits. Dated policies, programme descriptions and reported activity were analysed separately. Academic literature contextualized the comparison; heterogeneous patient and expenditure indicators were not pooled. Results The documents describe different allocations of authority. Japan links patient reception to accreditation and travel coordination; South Korea combines promotion with provider registration and liability insurance. Singapore places explicit limits on public hospitals’ recruitment of foreign patients. The Thai sources describe health authorities’ promotional roles, wellness assessment and a hospital–insurer payment process. India coordinates tourism, health, accreditation and visa functions through a national strategy and interministerial activity. These instruments provide different forms of information and accountability, but do not establish their effects on patient trust or safety. Shanghai already specifies insurance cooperation, complaints and statistical monitoring. Its published activity figures, like those for Boao Lecheng, do not isolate inbound medical tourists or demonstrate continuity after patients return home. Conclusions The comparison identifies where responsibilities are assigned and where implementation evidence remains incomplete. For China, priorities include distinguishing patient populations, evaluating existing safeguards and specifying responsibility at transitions between providers, insurers and jurisdictions. Additional national promotion alone would not resolve these questions.

items.title: Prevalence and Risk Factors of Child Sexual Abuse in Early Childhood Across Africa: A Protocol for a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Child sexual abuse (CSA) in early childhood represents a significant public health issue and a critical concern regarding children's rights, with profound lifelong consequences. Despite the growing recognition of CSA as a severe form of child maltreatment, its prevalence and impact in Africa remain poorly understood, primarily due to underreporting and fragmented evidence. Existing studies have predominantly focused on broader populations of children and adolescents, thereby limiting our understanding of the prevalence and risk factors associated with CSA in early childhood. To address this knowledge gap, this systematic review and meta-analysis will examine the prevalence and risk factors of CSA among children aged 8 years and younger across Africa. Methods: The protocol adheres to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Protocols guidelines. We will conduct a systematic search of seven scientific databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, African Journals Online, African Index Medicus, and Google Scholar) for studies published between January 1, 2016, and January 1, 2026. In addition, we will search for grey literature, including reports from UNICEF, the WHO Violence Against Children Surveys, and relevant government and institutional sources. Eligible studies will comprise observational studies (including cross-sectional studies cohort, and case control studies), randomized controlled trials (baseline data only), and mixed-methods studies that provide extractable quantitative data on the prevalence or risk factors of CSA among children aged 8 years and younger. Two independent reviewers will conduct screening, data extraction, and risk of bias assessment using tools from the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools, while the ROBINS-I framework will be applied to any non-randomized interventional designs where appropriate. A random-effects meta-analysis utilizing Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation will be performed for prevalence data. Heterogeneity will be assessed using I² and χ² statistics, and subgroup analyses and meta-regression will be conducted as feasible. Publication bias will be assessed through funnel plots and Egger's test. In instances where meta-analysis is not possible, a structured narrative synthesis will be performed. Discussion: This review will address a critical gap in early childhood research across Africa to highlight a frequently overlooked public health concern. Addressing this evidence gap is critical to strengthening early prevention and detection efforts, informing policy and resource allocation, and supporting the development of contextually appropriate child protection systems across the continent. Registration: PROSPERO (CRD420251085203)

items.title: Five-Year Longitudinal Changes and Determinants of Serum PFAS Exposure Profiles in a Community-Based Cohort from Southern China
items.abstract: Abstract Background Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants widely detected in human populations. Although regulatory actions have restricted several legacy PFAS, longitudinal evidence on changes in human PFAS exposure and their determinants remains limited, particularly in rapidly urbanizing regions. This study aimed to characterize five-year changes in serum legacy PFAS concentrations and identify demographic and geographic determinants of longitudinal exposure among community residents in Guangzhou, southern China. Methods We conducted a prospective community-based cohort study of 958 residents from three communities representing distinct residential environments: an urban commercial area, an industrial/livestock/fishery area, and an ecological conservation area. Participants were examined at baseline (2018–2019) and follow-up (2023–2024). Serum legacy PFAS concentrations were measured using ultra-performance liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry. Temporal changes were assessed using paired analyses, and longitudinal determinants were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models with false discovery rate correction. Results Six legacy PFAS with detection frequencies approaching 100% were included in longitudinal analyses. Over five years, total PFOS, PFNA, PFDA, and total PFHxS concentrations decreased from 14.129 to 11.262, 0.998 to 0.871, 0.692 to 0.532, and 0.771 to 0.598 ng/mL, respectively, whereas PFOA increased from 5.534 to 9.789 ng/mL and PFHpA from 0.024 to 0.034 ng/mL. Older age was consistently associated with higher concentrations of all six PFAS. Residential location was also an important determinant, with higher PFAS concentrations observed among residents of the urban commercial and industrial/livestock/fishery communities than among those in the ecological conservation community. Conclusions Serum legacy PFAS exposure showed heterogeneous five-year trajectories in this community-based population in Guangzhou, with divergent temporal patterns across individual PFAS. The contrasting trends and persistent demographic and geographic differences highlight the complexity of human PFAS exposure following regulatory changes. Continued biomonitoring and identification of populations with elevated exposure are warranted to support targeted exposure reduction and public health surveillance.

items.title: Youth Firearm Victimization in Philadelphia: Trends and Disparities Among Middle and High School Aged Youth
items.abstract: Abstract Urban firearm violence remains a critical public health crisis, with adolescents, especially high-school-aged youth and young men of color, disproportionately affected compared with younger children. However, limited research distinguishes patterns of victimization between middle school–aged youth (11–13) and high school–aged youth (14–18), despite important developmental and contextual differences between these groups. This study examines annual, monthly, weekly, and hourly patterns among 16,229 shooting incidents in Philadelphia from 2015 to 2024, comparing demographic characteristics, temporal trends, and fatality outcomes across the two age categories. Chi-squared analysis revealed significant associations between race and sex, with Black males comprising the majority of victims, particularly among 14–18-year-olds (89.0%). Temporal trends showed pandemic-era surges peaking in 2021, followed by substantial declines by 2024. Age-stratified analysis demonstrated higher average fatality rates among 14–18-year-olds (14.9%) compared to 11–13-year-olds (10.2%), indicating greater severity among high-school-aged youth. By directly comparing these age groups, this study highlights distinct developmental vulnerability periods and informs targeted, school-aligned violence prevention strategies.

items.title: Employment-type inequalities in healthy working life expectancy in China: evidence from CHARLS, 2011–2018
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Healthy working life expectancy (HWLE) has become an important metric for evaluating the feasibility and equity of extended working lives. In China, ongoing retirement-age reform is occurring within a labour market characterized by significant differences in physical demands, social protection, and exit pathways across agricultural work, self-employment, and wage employment. This study estimated employment-type inequalities in HWLE among older Chinese adults. Methods: We analysed pooled person-wave data from the 2011, 2013, 2015, and 2018 waves of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. The analytic sample included 34,644 person-wave observations from 11,626 adults aged 50–100 years. Four joint health-work states were defined by functional health and current work status: healthy-working, healthy-not working, unhealthy-working, and unhealthy-not working. Employment type was classified as agricultural work, self-employment, or family-business work, and employee or other work using CHARLS work-module variables. Sex- and employment-type-specific age prevalence in each state was combined with sex-specific United Nations life-table person-years to estimate state-specific expectancies from age 50. An illustrative value analysis examined how retirement-age conclusions changed when unhealthy work was assigned a lower value. Results: Remaining life expectancy at age 50 was fixed at 27.11 years for men and 31.76 years for women. Among men, healthy-working life expectancy ranged from 17.12 years among employees or other workers to 18.91 years among agricultural workers, while unhealthy-working life expectancy was highest among agricultural workers (4.00 years). Among women, agricultural workers had the least favourable profile, with the lowest healthy-working life expectancy (16.06 years) and the highest unhealthy-working expectancy (7.65 years). Self-employed or family-business women had the highest healthy-working life expectancy (20.78 years) and the lowest unhealthy-working expectancy (3.22 years). Under the illustrative value specification, welfare-maximising ages differed by sex and employment type. Conclusions: Employment type significantly influences the distribution of later life between healthy work, unhealthy work, and non-work in China. Evaluating retirement-age reform solely on the basis of average longevity is insufficient. A public health approach should account for the unequal burden of unhealthy work, particularly among women in agricultural employment.

items.title: From Hippocrates to UTCI: Twenty-Five Centuries of Human Biometeorology
items.abstract: Abstract Human biometeorology, which describes how the atmosphere and the wider environment affect human health, well - being, and performance, was initially organized and presented as a 20th-century discipline, formalized by Tromp and Landsberg and later by physiological thermal indices such as the Physiologically Equivalent Temperature (PET) and the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI). This paper takes a longer view. It traces a continuous, if uneven, tradition of linking atmospheric conditions to human health across more than two millennia: religious and mythological ideas, the weather knowledge of indigenous societies, biblical and ancient Near Eastern sources, the medical systems of Egypt, China and India, Presocratic natural philosophy, the Hippocratic Corpus, Aristotle and the Peripatetic school, and Hellenistic and Roman scholarship. It also argues that the thermal environment is not only something scholarship later described, but a force that helped shape culture itself - visible in the thermal picture of paradise and hell across unrelated traditions and in the open - air institutions of Greek public life. On the modern side, we place the decisive physical step earlier than usual: Konrad Büttner formulated the energy balance of the human body in the 1930s, three decades before Fanger and six before PET, and Wolf H. Weihe stated in 1976 the problem that still governs the field: especially the atmosphere acts through many factors, and their ranking depends on the question asked. Modern rational indices quantify a long-standing insight rather than inventing it: human health depends on several atmospheric factors acting together, not on air temperature alone.

items.title: First-line treatment of non-haemorrhagic early miscarriage in gynaecological emergencies in public hospitals on Reunion Island in 2022
items.abstract: Abstract Introduction: The prevalence of early spontaneous pregnancy loss (ESPL) is 12% for all pregnancies combined, and can be managed surgically or non-surgically. Non-surgical treatment is possible with in-town care. Health insurance reimbursement records revealed that the quotation for ESPL management in towns was very scarcely used in Reunion Island. Patients could benefit from more comprehensive care if they were seen in a local practice rather than in a hospital. However, the number of patients treated in hospital is unknown in Reunion Island. The primary outcome was to determine the first-line treatment preferred by patients with non-haemorrhagic ESPL in public hospitals in Reunion Island in 2022. Method: This cross-sectional descriptive study involved several hospital centres, with retrospective collection by review of gynaecological emergency department records from public hospitals in Reunion Island. Results: From January to December 2022, 947 patients were included in the four public hospitals of Reunion Island. Results varied slightly between centres. Non-surgical treatment as first-line therapy was chosen by 84 to 99% of women, depending on the centre; 42 to 69% received expectant management and 25 to 46% received pharmacological management (misoprostol). One to 16% of patients preferred immediate surgical management. The average timing of patient visits was mid-day. Conclusion: ESPL were largely treated by a non-surgical method as first-line treatment in public hospitals of Reunion Island in 2022. This encourages the creation of an out-of-hospital care network by the healthcare professionals concerned.

items.title: Patients’ Perceptions and Experiences of Medical Laboratory Service Quality in the Kumasi Metropolis, Ghana: A Convergent Parallel Mixed-Methods Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background : In recent years, laboratory services have become a significant feature of health care delivery in many developing countries. In Ghana, laboratory service provision has increased across private and public facilities. The study examined patients’ perceptions of quality and their experiences with medical laboratory services in the Kumasi metropolis, Ghana. Methods: The study employed a convergent parallel mixed-methods design. A survey of five hundred and thirty-nine (539) patients accessing medical laboratory services at Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH), Ghana Health Service, Christian Health Association of Ghana (CHAG), Private Hospitals and Private Standalone Laboratories was conducted from 8th March to 26th November 2021. The Service Quality (SERVQUAL) model was used to measure patients' perceptions of laboratory service quality across the five dimensions of Reliability, Assurance, Tangibility, Empathy, and Responsiveness. In addition, fourteen (14) in-depth interviews were conducted with patients to explore perspectives on the provision of quality medical laboratory services. SERVQUAL was calculated as the difference between perception and expectation for each dimension; a negative score indicates dissatisfaction, while a positive score indicates satisfaction. Descriptive statistics and quantile regression analysis were conducted to examine patient-related factors that influence perceptions. Qualitative data were analyzed thematically, and relevant statements were quoted verbatim. Results : Quantitative findings: The study included 539 patients; 30.2% were male, and 69.8% were female. Patients’ expectations exceeded their perceptions of laboratory service quality, with an overall SERVQUAL score of -0.60. The largest gap (-0.66) was in the Responsiveness dimension, and the smallest (-0.57) was in the Assurance dimension. Facility type and sex were significantly associated with patients’ perceptions of laboratory service quality. Patients were more satisfied with laboratory service quality in private health facilities than in Government facilities (β = 0.26; 95% CI: 0.04-0.47; p = 0.02). Similarly, females were more satisfied with service quality than male participants (β = 0.23, 95% CI: 0.04, 0.41, p = 0.02). Qualitative findings: Patients expressed dissatisfaction with the timeliness of results, the unavailability of requested tests, and the lack of communication and feedback. Conclusion : Patients rated services favourably, but expectations consistently exceeded the service experience, with the largest gap in Responsiveness.

items.title: Dietary Non-adherence and Associated Factors among Adults with Type 2 Diabetes in Ethiopia: A Sequential Explanatory Mixed- Methods Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Diabetes mellitus (DM) is one of the leading causes of death globally and the most rapidly growing cause of health loss. Current evidence strongly suggests that lifestyle changes, along with weight reduction, seem to overcome the genetic risk of the disease in individuals with pre-diabetes or recent type 2 DM. Despite efforts, adherence to dietary recommendations remains limited in Ethiopia. Methods Sequential explanatory mixed methods were employed, with a quantitative cross-sectional study, followed by semi-structured interviews in public health facilities in Shaggar City. For the quantitative phase, 588 type 2 diabetic patients were selected using systematic random sampling. Quantitative data were summarized using descriptive statistics, and logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with non-adherence to dietary recommendations. Qualitative data were analyzed using a thematic analysis approach. Results The magnitude of non-adherence to dietary recommendations was 68.90% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 64.9%, 72.8%). In multivariable logistic regression, household food insecurity (Adjusted Odds Ratio (AOR) = 4.04; 95% CI ( 2.07, 7.90), poor dietary knowledge (AOR = 2.14; 95% CI:(1.28–3.58), poor family support (AOR = 4.23; 95% CI: (2.44–7.31), normal body weight (AOR = 0.37, 95% CI (0.18–0.77), overweight (AOR = 0.41, 95% CI: (0.18–0.92) compared to obese, less than five years of follow-up (AOR = 2.56, 95% CI: (1.26–5.17), not receiving printed nutritional health education materials (AOR = 2.51; 95%CI: (1.31–4.81), and not accessing audio visual nutritional education (AOR = 1.98; 95%CI: (1.003–3.93) were significantly associated with non-adherence to dietary recommendations. Thematic analysis revealed that financial constraints, inflation, poor dietary knowledge, sedentary lifestyle, poor family support, and recent diagnosis of diabetes were barriers to adherence to dietary recommendations. Conclusions The magnitude of non-adherence to dietary recommendations was high, with multiple individual, household, and healthcare-related factors. Qualitative findings further highlighted economic constraints, sedentary lifestyle, and poor knowledge as key barriers, underscoring the need for multifaceted interventions to improve dietary adherence among diabetic patients.

items.title: Disparity in the Prevalence of Pit and Fissure Sealants Among 12-Year-Old Children in Puerto Rico: A Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Pit and fissure sealants (PFS) are an important tool in preventing and managing caries development on primary and permanent posterior teeth in children and adolescents. Among children living in Puerto Rico, particularly those of low socioeconomic status, this preventive measure has historically been underutilized. The completion of the Government Health Insurance (GHI) reform in 2000 marked a pivotal moment, expanding access to PFS across the entire island. In this study, we compared oral health data from 12-year-old school-attending children in Puerto Rico in 1997 and 2011 to evaluate changes in PFS prevalence and socioeconomic disparities, using school type as a proxy for socioeconomic status. Methods This cross-sectional study used two probabilistic samples (n = 1,587 in 2011 and n = 1,435 in 1997) of 12-year-olds enrolled in school, stratified by GHI region, school type, and sex. Calibrated examiners evaluated the presence of PFS on at least one permanent first molar. Logistic regression models compared PFS prevalence by school type in 1997 and 2011, adjusting for sex and region. A P -value ≤ 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results Sex distribution and school type were similar in 1997 (49% female; 18% private schools) and 2011 (53% female; 23% private schools). Between 1997 and 2011, PFS prevalence increased among all children (4.3% vs. 18.1%), as well as among children attending private (11.1% vs. 25.8%), public rural (3.4% vs. 16.3%), and public urban schools (2.5% vs. 16.9%). Participants attending public-rural and public-urban schools were less likely to have sealants, both in 1997 ( OR public−rural =0.19; 95% CI: 0.07–0.46; OR public−urban =0.17; 95% CI: 0.06–0.48) and in 2011 ( OR public−rural =0.57; 95% CI: 0.33–0.99; OR public−urban =0.60; 95% CI: 0.39–0.93), versus those from private schools. Conclusions PFS prevalence increased among 12-year-old school-attending children in Puerto Rico across all school types between 1997 and 2011, a period that coincided with island-wide GHI implementation. However, disparities between children attending public and private schools persisted. These findings suggest that expanded insurance coverage alone may be insufficient to eliminate disparities in preventive dental care and that socioeconomic background may influence PFS utilization.

items.title: Beyond a Decade of MENACTRIMS: Scientific Achievements, Publicly Documented Implementation Gaps, and a Roadmap to a Regional Learning Health System
items.abstract: Background: The Middle East North Africa Committee for Treatment and Research in Multiple Sclerosis (MENACTRIMS) has developed congresses, clinical guidance, registry research, training, certification, and advocacy partnerships. Evaluating this infrastructure requires distinctions between organizational activity, implementation, and attributable benefit. Objectives: To characterize documented achievements, compare the geographic distribution of major functions, identify public reporting gaps, and propose a measurable regional learning-health-system roadmap. Methods: A structured public-document audit and targeted literature synthesis covered activities from 2014 through 23 August 2026, with a documented update on 16 October 2026. Sources were classified by provenance and evidentiary purpose, without performance scoring. Geographic coverage used a fixed 19-jurisdiction Middle East and North Africa frame. Reported attendance terms and registry denominators were preserved. Results: Ten completed congresses were identified; seven with exact headline attendance had a median of 934 participants (interquartile range 761.5–1006.5). Seven congresses were hosted in the United Arab Emirates. Five major guideline outputs or revisions, multicountry registry studies, policy endorsements, and traceable grant- and fellowship-linked publications demonstrated sustained scientific activity. The public registry headline was 15,387, compared with 14,438 enumerable center records; variable displays represented 78.8%–93.9% of the headline, without establishing true field completeness. Iran, Egypt, and Kuwait contributed 75.4% of enumerable records. Council listings covered 15/19 jurisdictions, registry centers 8/19, and certified centers 2/19. Certification standards already specify three-year renewal and prefer registry participation; fellowship terms require reporting and career follow-up. Aggregated results of these processes were less readily ascertainable. Conclusions: MENACTRIMS has established substantial regional infrastructure. Differing geographic distributions identify questions about coordination and opportunity but do not establish organizational failure. A phased roadmap for 2027–2035 should build on existing systems through denominator reconciliation, publicly reported program outcomes, guideline-linked quality improvement, and meaningful patient and professional participation. Public-source limitations and the non-systematic synthesis preclude causal attribution of regional patient outcomes to MENACTRIMS.

items.title: Differences in Antibiotic Use Practices Among Children with Diarrhea in Urban and Rural Bangladesh
items.abstract: Background: Misuse and overuse of antibiotics in childhood diarrhea pose a high risk of antimicrobial resistance (AMR), which is a public health threat globally, and Bangladesh is no exception. This study aims to describe urban-rural differences and determine the factors associated with antibiotic use at home in children before seeking care for diar-rhea at the health care facilities. Methods: This cross-sectional study, over an 18-month period, included 5,894 children aged 1-59 months from two large health facilities: a rural secondary-level district hospital, located in Tangail, and an urban diarrhea specialized facility, icddr,b Dhaka hospital. Following clinical care, trained staff used a pre-validated structured questionnaire to collect data on child demographics, clinical symptoms, feeding practices, and treatment received prior to hospital visit. The primary outcome was antibiotic use at home before hospital presentation. Multivariable logistic regression models analyzed factors linked to home antibiotic use. Results: The preva-lence of antibiotic use at home before seeking care among diarrheal children was sig-nificantly higher in children visiting a rural facility as compared to that of the urban facility (90.0% vs. 68.4%). Pharmacies were the primary source of antibiotics for children in both rural and urban areas (64.1% vs. 61.2%). Multivariable analysis showed that in urban settings, children with diarrhea for 1-3 days were more than twice as likely (aOR:2.39, 95% CI:1.66.4), and those sick for 4 or more days were three times as likely (aOR:3.09, 95% CI: 2.21–4.43) to receive antibiotics at home compared to children who had less than one day of diarrhea. Children with no history of a prior hospital visit for diarrhea were also 1.86 times at higher risk of using antibiotics (aOR: 1.86, 95% CI:1.28–2.72). In a rural setting, children with diarrhea for 1–3 days had five times (aOR:5.11, 95% CI: 3.6–7.1), and those who had diarrhea for 4 days or more had two times higher odds (aOR: 1.97, 95% CI: 1.43–2.73) for antibiotic use. Moreover, children whose caregivers used ORS were 2.8 times more likely to use antibiotics at home (aOR:2.80, 95% CI: 1.06-7.35). Conclusions: This study demonstrates that antibiotic use at home before seeking care is alarmingly high among children with diarrhea in Bangladesh, particu-larly in rural settings, driven by informal pharmacy access and symp-tom-duration-driven decision-making in urban areas. This emphasizes the need to en-hance awareness in both sectors of the public and healthcare providers. Moreover, im-plementing and monitoring strict regulations for antibiotic sales over-the-counter in pharmacies is essential to impede escalating trends of AMR in Bangladesh.

items.title: Guaraci: A Reproducible Orchestrator for Direct Extraction of Brazilian Public-Health and Environmental Data
items.abstract: Brazilian public data relevant to health and the environment are dispersed across heterogeneous official systems - FTP servers (DATASUS), REST APIs (OpenDataSUS/DEMAS), and web portals (gov.br) - and published in legacy, often compressed formats (e.g., DBC/DBF) with schemas that change across years and topics, which makes integrated, reproducible reuse costly. Guaraci is an open-source (MIT), Docker-first orchestrator that acquires such data directly from the primary official sources, decodes legacy formats, harmonizes heterogeneous schemas, records full provenance, and delivers the result to a downstream data lake. It integrates 90+ sources spanning public health (DATASUS microdata such as hospital and mortality information system; OpenDataSUS arbovirus and immunization data; gov.br sanitation indicators) and the environment (NASA POWER climate series, FIRMS active-fire detections and GPM IMERG precipitation), behind a single asynchronous job engine exposed through a command-line interface and a REST API. Data are decoded to records with pyreaddbc/dbfread, harmonized by taking the union of all historical columns (null-padding missing fields) and exported to CSV, Parquet and SQLite with a machine-readable file capturing source, request filters and output paths. By abstracting unstable FTP servers, paginated APIs and legacy encodings behind one reproducible mechanism, Guaraci lowers the technical barrier to Brazilian public data and continuously supplies analysis-ready inputs for spatio-temporal epidemiological modelling, machine-learning applications and cross-source studies.

items.title: Claims-based frailty, dual eligibility, and potential unmet home-health needs in older breast cancer survivors.
items.abstract: Older breast cancer survivors often need home-based functional support, yet whether Medicare's restricted home health (HH) benefit leaves frailty-related need unmet at the population level is not quantified because measurement is lacking. Using linked Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results-Medicare-OASIS data, we studied 347 953 survivor-years during 2017-2020 from 134 410 women with invasive breast cancer 2-10 years post-diagnosis. We derived a claims-based predicted deficit-accumulation frailty index (DAFI), calibrated by penalized elastic-net to the observed OASIS Start-of-Care DAFI, the HH-need benchmark. Outcomes were any Medicare HH use and potential unmet need, defined as no HH use among high-need survivor-years (predicted DAFI ≥ 0.25). Logistic models estimated the marginal effects of DAFI on any Medicare HH use by frailty and dual eligibility, and disparities in potential unmet need. The claims-based DAFI was closely calibrated to observed OASIS DAFI (area under the curve = 0.715; slope = 1.111). Any HH use rose with frailty (+1.10 percentage points [pp] per +0.01 DAFI; 95% CI = 1.05 to 1.15), most steeply among never-dual survivors (+1.21 pp; 95% CI = 1.16 to 1.26) and less steeply among always-dual survivors (+0.41 pp; 95% CI = 0.30 to 0.53). Among high-need survivor years, 59.6% had no Medicare HH use. Long-term survivors had similar DAFI to 2-5-year survivors (0.216 vs 0.215) and lower HH use, but potential unmet need did not differ. A claims-based frailty proxy reveals potential frailty-related needs that Medicare HH does not reach. Expanding Medicare HH to better cover personal care and other home- and community-based services may help address frailty-related needs.

items.title: RESULT-Hip. The impact of restrictive compared with liberal transfusion strategy on cardiac injury and death in patients undergoing surgery for hip fracture : protocol for a multicentre, randomized controlled trial of two blood transfusion strategies.
items.abstract: Hip fracture is a global health issue. Complications are common, leading to reduced quality of life or death. These occur more frequently if anaemia is present. We hypothesize that correcting anaemia in the perioperative period may decrease major adverse cardiac events (MACE) and death after hip fracture. This multicentre prospective randomized trial compares transfusion strategies after hip fracture in patients aged ≥ 60 years. We initially planned to randomize 1,984 participants with anaemia, defined as haemoglobin ≤ 90 g l-1, to one of two transfusion strategies: liberal transfusion (aim haemoglobin 90 g l-1 to 110 g l-1), or restrictive transfusion (aim 75 g l-1 to 90 g l-1). The intervention lasts from randomization to hospital discharge or 30 days post randomization, whichever is soonest. The primary outcome measure was a composite of death or MACE adjudicated by blinded clinical experts. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality and quality of life, evaluated at 120 days. Cost-effectiveness and health economic evaluation will also be reported. This trial was funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research, HTA award (National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) 130875) and registered at ISRCTN 28818784. Ethical approval was obtained to recruit patients in the UK. As recruitment fell short of the initial target, and following consultation with the funder, we refined our primary outcome to include myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery (MINS), and reduced the required sample size to 842. Recruitment commenced on 10 June 2022. The first participant was recruited on 16 June 2022. We will engage clinicians and healthcare planners to implement the findings. We plan to recruit until 31 October 2026. Results will be disseminated to clinicians, policymakers, patients, and the public.
