items.title: Traditional Ethnic Beverages as Sources of Phenolic Compounds: Antioxidant and Anti-inflammatory Properties—A Narrative Review
items.abstract: Indigenous groups have been consuming traditional ethnic beverages for generations, and they play a significant role in their dietary customs, cultural legacy, and traditional medical systems.These drinks are typically made using naturally occurring fermentation processes that improve the nutritional content and bioactive composition of cereals, fruits, herbs, and other locally accessible plant materials.Traditional fermented drinks are rich in phenolic compounds, flavonoids, organic acids, bioactive peptides, and beneficial microbes, which together support a variety of biological activities, according to mounting scientific data.Because of their ability to avoid oxidative stress and chronic inflammatory illnesses, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory capabilities have garnered significant interest.Fermentation increases the bioavailability and biological effectiveness of phytochemicals by facilitating their release and biotransformation.In experimental studies, a number of traditional beverages, such as Haria, Kanji, Pakhoi, Chubitchi, Makgeolli, Judima, and other native fermented drinks, have shown notable free radical scavenging activity, inhibition of lipid peroxidation, modulation of inflammatory cytokines, and regulation of oxidative stress pathways.However, due to variations in raw ingredients, fermentation techniques, microbial variety, and geographic origin, there is a great deal of variation in their phytochemical content and biological activities.The present understanding of the phenolic composition, antioxidant capacity, and anti-inflammatory potential of traditional ethnic beverages is summarized in this narrative review, with a focus on beverages that the Khasi population of Meghalaya, India, typically consumes.Furthermore, it highlights the underlying mechanisms responsible for their biofunctional properties, discusses existing research gaps, and outlines future perspectives for the scientific validation and development of traditional ethnic beverages as evidence-based functional foods.

items.title: Spatial and temporal patterns of human-elephant conflict and compensation in Nagaon District, Assam, India
items.abstract: Human-elephant conflict (HEC) threatens both biodiversity and rural livelihoods. Forest departments in affected districts hold decades of compensation-claim records, but these archives are seldom analyzed for the spatial and temporal insights they contain. This study analyses twenty-one years of compensation-claim records from Nagaon District, Assam, India (1999–2020) to identify the spatial, seasonal, and institutional structure of conflict, and to assess whether compensation is allocated in proportion to the burden it addresses. Getis-Ord Gi* and Local Moran’s I statistics were applied to 1,915 georeferenced incidents across 1,032 villages, and 1,788 records with complete financial data were examined using non-parametric correlation, Theil-Sen regression, and segmentation by policy regime. Conflict was reported in 241 villages (23.35%), with hotspots concentrated along the Karbi Anglong foothills and human casualty clusters localized in the northeastern part of the district. Incidents peaked in December (23.29%), coinciding with the Sali rice harvest. Property and crop damage together accounted for over 88% of claims but under 28% of disbursed funds, while human fatalities represented 6.26% of claims and 68.37% of funds. Claim volume explained only 31.8% of the variation in payouts, with compensation rate revisions accounting for most of the remainder. Mitigation should be spatially targeted and seasonally adaptive, and compensation restructured into a tiered, need-based model that recognizes chronic livelihood loss alongside catastrophic outcomes.

items.title: Genetic isolation and loss of diversity in the broadcast spawning coral, Acropora kenti at Yunbenun (Magnetic Island) on the Great Barrier Reef
items.abstract: Abstract Coral populations on inshore reefs of the Great Barrier Reef (GBR) face increasing pressures from environmental stressors. Genetic diversity and connectivity are key determinants of coral adaptive capacity. Acropora kenti forms at least four genetically distinct clusters distributed across hundreds of kilometres along the GBR. One cluster which is potentially vulnerable due to restricted geographic distribution is found at Yunbenun (Magnetic Island). Here, we conducted a genetic assessment of A. kenti populations from seven reefs around Yunbenun and eight adjacent inshore and mid-shelf reefs in the central GBR to identify their population structure, genetic diversity and connectivity. Using single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) we demonstrate that a genetically distinct (F st >0.33) lineage dominates at all bays around Yunbenun but is rarely found on adjacent reefs. Fine-scale analysis within the Yunbenun lineage revealed a pattern of isolation by distance, driven by limited gene flow. Admixture analysis supported by hydrodynamic modelling shows that larval dispersal is occurring between Yunbenun and surrounding reefs, but gene flow remains limited. Populations at Yunbenun have lower allelic richness ( p < 0.001) and much lower effective population sizes (N e = 1348 (northern bays), N e = 91 (southern bays)) compared with adjacent reefs (N e = 9494). These findings demonstrate that although the genetic diversity of A. kenti across the GBR remains high, isolated and potentially locally adapted populations such as those at Yunbenun may be at risk of genetic decline, undermining their adaptive potential and increasing their conservation concern.

items.title: Exports of technologically related environmental goods are associated with higher environmental performance in OECD countries
items.abstract: In this study, the impact of trade in technologically related environmental goods on environmental quality in OECD countries is examined for the period 2000–2023 using the MMQR method. To further address potential reverse causality concerns, the empirical analysis is complemented by the Dumitrescu–Hurlin panel Granger causality test. The study highlights how trade in these goods promotes the diffusion of environmentally friendly technologies, thereby supporting sustainable energy transitions and improvements in environmental performance. Empirical findings show that exports of technologically related environmental goods have a positive and significant impact across all quantiles, indicating that exports contribute consistently to technology diffusion. In contrast, the effect of imports becomes significant only in countries with relatively high environmental performance levels. The Dumitrescu–Hurlin test results further indicate a unidirectional predictive relationship running from both exports and imports of technologically related environmental goods to environmental performance, while no statistically significant feedback from environmental performance to trade variables is detected. The results further reveal that economic growth initially harms environmental quality, but as development progresses, its effect turns positive, confirming the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis. Renewable energy consumption provides limited short-term support for environmental performance, whereas urbanization generally exerts positive effects. Overall, the findings suggest that sustainable development policies should be tailored to country-specific structural characteristics. To maximize the benefits of trade in technologically related environmental goods, it is recommended that countries prioritize tax incentives encouraging the export of environmentally friendly products and invest in infrastructure that facilitates the effective domestic use of imported environmental technologies.

items.title: Microplastic contamination in commercially important marine fishes from the Sohar Coast, Sea of Oman: occurrence, characterization, and polymer composition
items.abstract: Microplastic (MP) pollution is an increasing concern in marine environments because of its persistence, bioavailability, and potential implications for marine ecosystem health and seafood safety. Despite growing global attention, information on MP contamination in commercially important marine fish from the Sea of Oman remains limited. This study assessed the occurrence, abundance, and characteristics of MPs in four commercially important fish species from the Sohar coast and tested whether MP contamination differed among species and tissues and was associated with habitat group, sex, and biometric characteristics. A total of 120 fish representing Epinephelus areolatus , Lethrinus microdon , Nematalosa arabica , and Rastrelliger kanagurta were examined for MPs in the gastrointestinal tract (GIT) and gills. Microplastics were extracted using alkaline digestion and visually identified under a stereomicroscope. All 316 recovered particles were subjected to ATR-FTIR spectroscopy; 313 (99.1%) met the ≥ 70% spectral-match criterion and were successfully assigned to polymer types. Microplastics were detected in 79.2% of the examined fish, with a mean total abundance of 2.63 ± 2.60 items individual⁻1. Frequency of occurrence ranged from 66.7% to 90.0% among species. Total MP abundance did not differ significantly among species, whereas GIT MP concentration differed significantly among species. GIT–gill differences were significant only in E. areolatus and R. kanagurta . No significant associations were detected between total MP abundance and habitat group, sex, total length, body weight, or condition factor. Fibers were the dominant particle type, most particles measured < 2 mm, and polyester was the predominant identified polymer, followed by polypropylene and ethylene-propylene diene polymer (EPDM). The predominance of fibers and polyester indicates that fibrous synthetic materials constitute an important component of MP exposure in these commercially important fishes. However, specific environmental sources cannot be determined from polymer identity alone, highlighting the need for integrated assessment of fish alongside seawater, sediments, and other potential environmental sources.

items.title: Constructing community economies: a pathway toward just agri-food transitions?
items.abstract: Exploring pathways toward just agri-food transitions has attracted increasing attention in political discourse and civic action. Community economies focus on alternative economic practices, reciprocity, and ethical commitments, aligning with the just transition goal of preventing new or intensified injustices in agri-food systems. This article develops a conceptual framework for analyzing the construction of community economies in agri-food systems and critically examines how economic alterity, performative interventions, and everyday practices can contribute to just transitions. Drawing on an in-depth case study of Mui Wo, an agricultural community in Hong Kong, this study investigates how a community economy model emerges, is constituted, and interacts with powerful actors and wider structural forces. The findings show that Mui Wo’s community economy has generated meaningful openings for a just agri-food transition, especially through recognition, community value chains, and capacity-building. However, government indifference to agriculture, structural constraints such as land ownership, insufficient support systems, and the absence of formal mechanisms for stakeholder participation in land-use decisions undermine the effectiveness of community economies in transforming agri-food systems. These findings highlight the need for transition interventions to re-examine policy frameworks and confront structural determinants, thereby empowering community economy pathways to advance just and sustainable transitions.

items.title: An asteroseismic age estimate for the Pleiades using a neural-network emulator of rotating δ Scuti pulsation models
items.abstract: Asteroseismology of δ Sct stars has strong potential for determining the ages of young stars through individual mode fitting. We present a neural-network emulator trained on approximately 46 million rotating pulsation models. From stellar mass, metallicity, age, and equatorial rotation velocity, it predicts 12 classical observables, two asteroseismic scalars, and the p mode, f mode and low-order g mode frequencies for degrees ℓ=0-3, including the individual m components of rotationally split multiplets. We couple the emulator to nested sampling through a multivariate likelihood that propagates correlated emulator residuals, making full Bayesian posterior exploration practical. Applied to five δ Sct stars in the Pleiades observed by TESS, the framework gives mutually consistent individual asteroseismic ages of 107-117 Myr. Combining their age posteriors gives a cluster age of 113.3±4.5 Myr (statistical), consistent with the 112±5 Myr lithium-depletion-boundary age and the 110-160 Myr range from rotating-isochrone fitting. Together with spectroscopic vsini, the inferred equatorial velocities also provide post-fit inclination estimates. Separate perturbed-grid tests using 100 matched synthetic pairs per input-physics variation give median absolute age shifts of 2.1, 2.3, and 5.2 Myr for |Δf_ov|=0.005, |Δα_MLT|=0.1, and |ΔY|=0.02, respectively; the corresponding 90th percentile shifts are 6.5, 7.6, and 16.2 Myr. These tests describe conditional population sensitivities, not a systematic uncertainty on the Pleiades age. Together, the cluster-age agreement and the scale of these input-physics sensitivities support δ Sct asteroseismology as a complementary age estimation method for young stars.

items.title: A chemically etched D-band waveguide orthomode transducer for CMB measurements
items.abstract: Abstract This study presents a prototype D-band waveguide orthomode transducer (OMT) fabricated using chemically etched brass platelets. This method offers a fast, cost-effective, and scalable approach for producing such devices above 100 GHz, making it well-suited for current and future Cosmic Microwave Background polarization experiments, where large focal planes with thousands of receivers are required to detect the faint primordial B -modes. Chemical etching has already demonstrated its effectiveness in manufacturing corrugated feedhorn arrays with state-of-the-art performance up to 150 GHz. Here, we evaluate its applicability to more complex structures, such as OMTs. We designed a single OMT prototype operating in the 130–170 GHz range, fabricated by chemically etching 0.15 mm-thick brass plates, which were then stacked, aligned, and mechanically clamped. Simulations based on metrological measurements of the OMT profile predict reflected power below −10 dB, cross-polarization better than −30 dB, and transmission around −0.5 dB in the 140−170 GHz band. Measurements yield transmisison around −1.5/−2 dB and cross-polarization $$<-$$ 20 dB. Further simulations show that the degradation in the transmission is related to defects and roughness along the etched profile ( $$\textrm{RMS}\simeq $$ 3 $$\mu $$ m), which is a typical and unavoidable effect of chemical etching. The discrepancy in cross-polarization, instead, could arise from a $$\sim $$ 1.5 $$^{\circ }$$ rotation of the polarization angle within the measurement chain. Our results show that chemical etching is a fast, low-cost, and scalable technique for producing waveguide OMTs with state-of-the-art performance in terms of reflected power and cross-polarization. However, at frequencies above 100 GHz our results show that the mechanical precision limitations of the chemical etching process degrade the transmission coefficient.

items.title: SpecLLM: LLM-based VNIR spectral interpretation
items.abstract: Abstract Visible and near-infrared (VNIR) spectroscopy identifies materials from characteristic spectral bands, and spectroscopists interpret spectra by features such as peak positions and intensities. Recent machine-learning and foundation models for hyperspectral data are highly effective but return numerical outputs or latent representations rather than such feature-level descriptions. Meanwhile, LLM-based spectral approaches have mostly provided raw numerical sequences. We present a method for making spectroscopic data accessible to large language models (LLMs) through compact, feature-based representations. Instead of supplying full spectra as comma-separated values (CSV), JavaScript Object Notation (JSON), or extensible markup language (XML), the proposed approach extracts summary statistics and discriminative extrema. It serialises them as either natural language or structured JSON. We evaluate prototype-based substance classification in two complementary scenes from an open-access VNIR hyperspectral blood dataset. For the selected models, compact feature representations were substantially more effective than raw numerical encodings, but less effective than a Random Forest operating on raw spectra. The natural-language format provides a human-readable, inspectable serialisation of compact spectral evidence and reduces prompt length compared with full-spectrum encodings. We also compared natural language and JSON feature representations and found them broadly comparable.

items.title: How Much Did the Moon-Forming Impact Change Earth's Core Fraction?
items.abstract: Earth's core, made mostly of iron, makes up about 32% of the planet's mass. In the giant-impact theory of the Moon's origin, a roughly Mars-sized planet, often called Theia, struck the young Earth and placed iron-poor rocky debris, mostly from the impactor, into orbit, where the Moon formed. The Moon has only a small iron core. What that impact did to the share of Earth's mass held in its own core depends on more than the impact itself, because two processes, each supported by published work, push in opposite directions. Collisions between bodies that already have iron cores can knock away rock more easily than iron, which raises the core's share. But models of Earth's core formation suggest that, as the planet grew, more of its iron combined with oxygen and stayed in the rocky mantle, which, this Commentary argues, lowers the core's share. Earth's iron-to-magnesium ratio is about 10% above the solar value, which has been interpreted as a net loss of about 10% of rock relative to metal over Earth's whole growth. A simple estimate suggests that the rock removed to form the Moon would raise Earth's core share by only a few percent of its value at most. Because the two processes oppose each other and other factors are unknown, the net change caused by the Moon-forming impact cannot yet be stated with confidence.

items.title: Contribution of Cosmic Alphas to Generation of Albedo Neutrons and Gammas in Lunar Regolith
items.abstract: The lunar surface is constantly and directly exposed to Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCRs) due to the lack of the atmosphere and the magnetic field around it. The high-energetic alpha particles subsequently contribute to the generation of the secondary neutrons through either the spallation reaction or the low-energetic (alpha, n) process along with the cosmic protons. In this study, the contribution of the alpha particles to the production of the albedo neutrons as well as the albedo gamma rays in the lunar regolith is studied by using the Monte Carlo simulations based on the GEANT4 toolkit. The incident alpha particles are referenced from the PAMELA spectrometer over the interval between 0.14 and 52 GeV and executed as a probability-based primary particle source. The present simulations demonstrate the production of the albedo neutrons and gamma rays upon the process of cosmic alpha irradiation in the lunar regolith. The albedo neutron production is predominantly situated within the near-surface region of the lunar regolith and progressively diminishes with the increasing depth. The population of the secondary neutrons is primarily distributed over the low-energy region and reduces towards the high energies. These results imply that the cosmic alpha particles have also quantifiable contribution in the generation of the secondary radiation at the lunar surface together with the cosmic protons, and this study demonstrates a computational framework in the evaluation of the lunar albedo, the radiation transport, the surface composition, and the radiation environment for the further lunar exploration missions.

items.title: Evidence-informed dynamic modelling and intervention prioritisation in diabetic bone marrow
items.abstract: Aims. Fragmented understanding of how diabetes disrupts interconnected bone marrow niches has hindered integrated strategies to restore function. Building on a previous static network, we developed a dynamic model to simulate intervention responses. Methods. The investigator and ChatGPT dialogued to extract evidence from a frozen corpus and develop the model. A Python implementation extended Boolean logic to three ordinal levels (0, 1 and 2) representing biological states and, where applicable, intervention strength. Under high metabolic stress, 15 interventions were assessed at three strengths and four with binary settings; 171 pairs were tested at maximal strength. A domain balanced score (0 to100) integrated favourable and adverse changes. Staged simulations assessed withdrawal; regulatory constraints on recovery after metabolic stress reduction were examined separately. Results. Endothelial reactive oxygen species (ROS) suppression achieved the highest score among 19 single interventions (24.2), improving three functional domains. Endothelial protein kinase B (Akt) augmentation scored 15.2 (two domains); oncostatin M (OSM) blockade and haematopoietic 66 kDa SHC transforming protein 1 (p66Shc) loss each scored 13.6 (two domains). ROS suppression combined with either OSM blockade or p66Shc loss scored 37.9, (five domains). No pair restored all functions under high stress. Benefits of ROS suppression, Akt augmentation and ROS and OSM blockade disappeared after withdrawal. Reducing metabolic stress led to variable scores (range 4.5 to 100), increasing mainly with restored endothelial function, followed by progenitor recovery and interruption of inflammatory and adipocyte stromal signalling. Conclusions. These simulations offer a rule based framework for investigating diabetic marrow recovery. Experimental studies must establish whether it can guide targeted therapy.

items.title: Longitudinal fMRI reveals multi-network reconfiguration and a recurrent frontoparietal shift across rest and task states during adult aging
items.abstract: Functional connectivity changes across adult aging, but most evidence is cross-sectional, and covariance-based connectivity depends on blood oxygenation level dependent (BOLD) fluctuation amplitude. Covariance decline can reflect changing fluctuation amplitude, and its interpretation may depend on whether normalization uses signal amplitude or includes estimated noise. It is also unclear which longitudinal changes recur across brain states. We analyzed 852 adults (baseline age 36-89 years) from the Aging Adult Brain Connectome with repeated functional MRI (fMRI) during rest, inhibitory control, associative memory, and visual-motor processing (2,220 sessions; median follow-up 5.5 years). Baseline age and elapsed follow-up were modeled separately. Ten cortical networks were tested jointly across states, and covariance was normalized either by released signal amplitude or by a candidate total amplitude reconstructed from released signal and noise amplitudes. Native common covariance declined by 7-11% per 5 years, while signal pair amplitude declined by 9% on average across states, significantly more than estimated noise pair amplitude. Under signal normalization, the relative balance among networks reconfigured over follow-up and differed across states, and the frontoparietal network shifted positively relative to the other nine networks in all four states, by 5-8% per 5 years. The estimated common trajectory was near zero under signal normalization but declined by 4-7% per 5 years under candidate total normalization. The network reconfiguration and the positive frontoparietal-relative direction persisted under both. Within-person coupling between the frontoparietal shift and fluid cognition was not detected. Adult aging thus combines normalization-dependent overall change with a state-dependent redistribution among networks that includes a recurrent frontoparietal shift.

items.title: Global stability of Michaelis-Menten networks
items.abstract: In a very nice paper, Blanchini, Breda, Giordano and Liessi studied networks of species coupled through Michaelis-Menten interactions. Under standard assumptions of strong connectedness and non-degeneracy, they show that there is a unique equilibrium, which is (locally) asymptotically stable. This note shows that global stability, which was stated there as an open problem, holds as well. In fact, whenever a positive equilibrium exists, it attracts every solution with positive initial condition, with no connectedness or non-degeneracy hypothesis at all; those assumptions are needed only in order to guarantee existence and to cover solutions starting on the boundary of the orthant. The key is to note that the system is contractive with respect to the Thompson part metric.

items.title: Single-Transit Parameter Estimation with Calibrated Uncertainties
items.abstract: The growing volume of photometric data from current and upcoming exoplanet surveys demands automated analysis pipelines to detect and characterize exoplanet transit signals. Among these, single-transit events present a challenge, since only one event is observed, and standard transit-fitting techniques for periodic signals do not directly apply because they rely on phase-folding. Beyond detection, characterizing these events is equally critical for follow-up, yet existing approaches are either sensitive to stellar variability and require prior detrending, or depend on stellar priors and per-target fitting. This work presents a convolutional neural network that predicts transit depth, duration, and mid-transit time, together with calibrated uncertainties, directly from a single transit signal. Our network is trained on synthetic light curves and evaluated against a trapezoidal least-squares baseline. On 120 confirmed exoplanets, both methods achieve comparable median errors, but the baseline fails to locate the transit in 10% of cases, producing unreliable estimates that would propagate into follow-up prioritization. In contrast, our network fails in only 1% of cases, yields lower mean absolute errors, and does not require detrending or stellar priors. Detrending would distort or remove the transit along with high stellar variability, precisely where the baseline fails and our network succeeds. Finally, we identify 169 new transit candidates in TESS Sectors 27-60 and apply our approach to obtain their physical parameters, creating a catalog that includes single-transit, multi-transit and multi-planet systems. This approach offers a scalable path toward automated characterization of single transit events, a population that will grow with upcoming surveys.

items.title: A general mechanism for collective foraging: percolating recruitment cascades coupled to a maximum-entropy
items.abstract: Foraging recruitment is a contagion: an agent finding a resource triggers a linear-threshold cascade -- the model for rumour and adoption spread on social networks -- embedded in space. Because activation is degree-normalized, the same rule that spreads the cascade also stifles it as neighbourhoods crowd (density-dependent blocking), so the swarm aggregates on a resource, then releases to explore again. The cascade runs on the communication network, but acting on it moves agents in physical space, and that motion rewires the network: network and physical space are one coupled system, and this feedback -- not tuning -- makes the coordination self-limiting. Because recruitment chains along the graph rather than near neighbours alone, whether a discovery stays local or spans the swarm is a matter of percolation, and past a critical connectivity the swarm holds itself in a cascade window -- locally near-critical though globally subcritical, a self-organized, sandpile-like drive-avalanche cycle. Nothing is tuned, yet behaviours foraging biology documents separately emerge together -- recruitment, marginal-value patch-leaving, and Levy search with a switch to local exploitation. These are not coincidences but one least-committal principle: the resource field and the search both follow from maximum entropy -- Levy search matched to the field's sparsity, recruitment to its clustering, so active-matter order and optimal foraging are one system in two domains. The gains are real but conditional: up to 7.6x the harvest of solitary search when resources are sparse and clustered, shrinking to nothing when search is already easy. Percolating cascades yield a large return on minimal communication. And that sparse, clustered field is the generic one -- resources almost inevitably aggregate, and maximum entropy makes it the least-committal one once they do -- so one untuned rule should recur widely.

items.title: Modeling the Coevolution of Human Skills and AI Adoption
items.abstract: The value of relying on generative AI depends on two quantities that evolve with its use: users' unaided skill, which may decline without practice, and the originality of AI-assisted work, which may decline as more people rely on similar tools. We model this process as a coevolutionary game in which individuals choose between autonomous and AI-assisted work, with autonomous practice strengthening their skills while reliance on AI gradually erodes them. When the reinforcing effect of skill erosion outweighs the crowding cost of lost originality, the population exhibits two alternative stable states: low AI adoption with high average skill, and high AI adoption with low average skill. Because skill is individual, autonomous workers remain more skilled than AI users, making autonomous work less vulnerable to population-wide skill decline. The strength of this effect is governed by a timescale ratio: the rate at which skills adapt relative to the rate at which individuals change strategy. The same ratio determines the full distribution of skills, which we derive analytically. Populations with identical AI adoption and average skill can differ sharply: when strategies change frequently, skills remain homogeneous and collective lock-in to high AI adoption is stronger; when strategies persist, lock-in weakens but the population can polarize into highly skilled autonomous workers and AI-dependent individuals. Modeling output overlap further shows that more diverse AI outputs can make widespread adoption harder to reverse. Together, these results expose tradeoffs between the benefits of widespread AI adoption and its long-run risks, making collective lock-in and skill polarization distinct intervention targets.

items.title: Strategic Origins of Network Structure
items.abstract: The structure and dynamics of complex networks are intimately linked. Despite immense progress in statistically characterizing these systems, a generalized mechanistic framework explaining why specific mesoscale structures emerge remains elusive. Here we introduce the game-graph equilibrium, the stable rest point of a payoff-driven partner-choice dynamic, analogous to a Nash equilibrium. This reveals network structure as the fossilized record of strategic interaction. We prove analytically that two-type games have exactly four network topologies, which are their exhaustive thermodynamic phases: assortative, disassortative, and two core-peripheries. This result generalizes to $K^K$ topological classes for $K$-type interactions. Furthermore, four distinct Nash equilibria produce core-periphery topologies, yet their payoffs reveal whether the underlying dynamic is cooperative or exploitative. To recover the generating dynamics from observed networks, we develop mechanistic inference by constraining a block model to lie on a low-dimensional, game-theoretic manifold. Applied to real-world networks, the model yields interpretable quantities, distinguishes states that look identical to conventional methods, predicts network topologies it has never seen without retraining, and controls its own complexity without hand-tuned penalties. Networks such as international trade are well described by the model despite the hard constraint, suggesting that real-world systems are organized by payoff-driven partner choice. Our framework resolves a foundational ambiguity by offering a precise, mechanistic definition of communities: strategic equivalence.

items.title: Mid-infrared Imaging of SR 12 c with JWST/MIRI: Grain Growth in an Evolved Circumplanetary Disk
items.abstract: The physical properties of circumplanetary disks offer insights into the formation of giant planets and their satellites. The circumbinary planetary-mass companion SR 12 c (1200 au from SR 12 AB) hosts an isolated dust disk directly detected with ALMA. We present JWST/MIRI imaging of SR 12 c from 5.6 to 21 $μ$m and analyze its spectral energy distribution from infrared to submillimeter wavelengths. Phenomenologically, the dust disk can be described by a two-component blackbody with large contrasts in characteristic temperatures and radii. Physically motivated models with varied geometries and heating mechanisms suggest a predominantly flat, irradiation-heated disk with a smaller contribution from viscous dissipation. The disk is inferred to be compact, with an inner radius of ~3 $R_{\rm Jup}$. The outer radius is only loosely constrained, with a characteristic value of ~3 au. The lack of strong 10 $μ$m excess emission suggests significant grain growth and dust settling. We also find that SR 12 c is broadly consistent with the empirical star-disk scaling relations, providing context for its possible formation pathway. These results demonstrate the power of combining mid-infrared and submillimeter observations with disk modeling to better understand the physical properties of circumplanetary disks.

items.title: Fabric retrofit scenario analysis under uncertainty for an urban housing stock using machine learning
items.abstract: Fabric retrofit is central to decarbonising housing, and planning it depends on expected savings and their uncertainty. This study asks which upgrade saves most per dwelling and across a housing portfolio, how uncertain the savings are, and whether upgrade order matters. We propose an uncertainty-aware framework that converts predicted changes in energy performance certificate scores after wall, roof and window upgrades into standardised energy-cost savings and emission reductions. Six machine-learning models predict the 1-100 Standard Assessment Procedure (SAP) energy-cost and environmental impact (EI) emission scores from 17 certificate descriptors. Each model's errors on similar dwellings give calibrated prediction intervals. A global-best strategy applies the most accurate model throughout; a sample-specific strategy chooses each dwelling's model using these local errors. The analysis covers 103,414 officially registered dwellings in Westminster, London. CatBoost was the global-best model, with mean absolute errors of 3.487 SAP and 4.379 EI points on held-out dwellings. Both strategies projected similar savings; under global-best, roof insulation saved most per dwelling, GBP 203 annually (uncertainty range 176-229), and wall insulation most across the portfolio, GBP 6.09 million annually (uncertainty range 5.69-6.72). For 5,382 dwellings needing all three upgrades, every order delivered the same final package, yet installing roofs, walls, then windows a year apart accumulated 54% more projected cost savings over three years than the reverse order. Emission reductions followed the same pattern. Using only certificate data, the framework helps local authorities rank measures for dwellings and portfolios and sequence upgrades to bring savings forward.

items.title: Linear Approximations Provide Rigorous Conditions for Phase Locking in Oscillator Networks and Power Grids
items.abstract: Synchronization is a fundamental collective phenomenon in many natural and engineered networks. The stable operation of oscillator networks, such as electric power grids, requires phase locking with phase differences across edges below a given threshold. A central question is whether a given network supports such a state. In this contribution, we extend a convex optimization formulation of the nonlinear fixed point equations of the Kuramoto model, that also describe lossless power grids. Based on this formulation, we derive rigorous and tight bounds on the error introduced by an arbitrary approximation of the original model, in particular linear approximations. The bounds yield edge-wise regions of trust around the approximation, within which the true nonlinear solution must lie. They further provide sufficient and necessary conditions for phase locking under prescribed phase difference limits. Numerical experiments show that the bounds are tight over a broad range of parameters.

items.title: Robustness of C/O and mean molecular weight under disequilibrium chemistry
items.abstract: Transmission spectroscopy increasingly reduces exoplanet spectra to derived compositional metrics, such as C/O, O/H, and mean molecular weight (MMW), but these quantities do not carry molecular abundance uncertainties in the same way. We assessed the reliability of these metrics for hot Jupiters and sub-Neptunes, by combining analytic uncertainty propagation with photochemical VULCAN forward models and representative published retrieval constraints. Propagating molecular abundance uncertainties produced substantially larger fractional uncertainties in elemental abundance ratios than in MMW. The fractional uncertainties in C/O and O/H were typically comparable to the inferred ratios, whereas the fractional uncertainty in MMW was more than two orders of magnitude smaller in H2/He-dominated atmospheres. Photochemistry and vertical mixing redistributed individual molecules but produced only minor changes in C/O and MMW at the pressures probed by transmission spectroscopy. C/O remains an important diagnostic of atmospheric chemistry and planetary formation history, but its interpretation requires careful uncertainty propagation. Mean molecular weight may provide a comparatively stable population-level diagnostic for linking observable atmospheres to bulk composition, especially across the sub-Neptune radius valley.

items.title: Radar and Infrasound Observations of the 2026 May 30 Cape Cod Bay Superbolide
items.abstract: Metre-scale impactors connect near-Earth-object dynamics, atmospheric-entry physics and meteorite delivery, but their pre-impact orbits and material properties are rarely measured together, especially for daylight events. We report observations of the 30 May 2026 Cape Cod Bay bolide. A very high frequency (VHF) meteor radar network detected atmospheric-entry plasma, weather radars detected falling meteorites, and infrasound sensors recorded the associated hypervelocity shock. VHF radar range--Doppler measurements resolve the meteor head echo from about 90 to 71 km altitude, while interferometric measurements localize short-lived non-specular plasma wake echoes down to an unusually low altitude of $\sim 30$ km. We identify this as the radar terminus, where breakup is expected to occur. A combined head-echo and trail fit constrains a steep southeastward trajectory over coastal Massachusetts. Weather-radar detections refine the dark-flight solution, place the likely fall region in Cape Cod Bay and constrain probable fragment sizes. Backward propagation of the fitted trajectory gives a heliocentric orbit near the cometary--asteroidal classification boundaries, with conflicting classifications from empirical dynamical criteria. Catalogue comparisons identify no convincing parent body or established meteor-shower association. Regional infrasound independently supports the terminal fragmentation region and yields an energy estimate of 0.5 kt TNT equivalent. The radar and dark-flight evidence are consistent with a dense, mechanically strong meteoroid, possibly iron-rich. The combination of meteor-radar plasma tracking, weather-radar observations of falling meteorites and infrasound measurements can provide accurate orbital elements and trace large meteoroids from atmospheric entry to nearly ground impact.

items.title: Optimal Trading Filters and the Value of Predictive Signals
items.abstract: The value of a forecast depends on its accuracy, but also on its actionability. In trading, an investor must translate return forecasts into positions while accounting for trading costs and the lingering impact of earlier trades. We solve the stationary quadratic trading problem with transient price impact using tools from prediction theory: Wiener-Hopf factorization gives the optimal policy as the composition of a conditional forecast and an explicit causal linear filter. We recover the Gârleanu-Pedersen aim-portfolio under exponential resilience and derive fractional trading filters under power-law impact decay, requiring memory beyond finite-dimensional LQR control. At fixed positive risk penalty, signals of equal instantaneous predictive strength have equal frictionless Markowitz value. With trading costs, net attainable value is determined by the mean square of the friction-weighted conditional forecast. Under power-law impact with exposure bleeding, we find an intermediate optimal mean-reversion rate for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck signals.

items.title: Granulation in Color: The Chromatic Stellar Flicker of LTT-9779 and WASP-121
items.abstract: Granulation is a persistent feature of stars with outer convective layers and is the photospheric signature of near-surface convective energy transport. In disk-integrated observations, it produces stochastic brightness variations that contribute substantially to stellar variability on timescales of minutes to hours. High-precision, observations with JWST provide an opportunity to study the chromatic signatures of stellar granulation. This work aims to measure the amplitude and characteristic timescale of granulation-induced variability for solar-type stars and to investigate whether the granulation signal shows significant chromatic variation in the near-infrared. We accessed publicly available JWST/NIRISS SOSS time-series observations of LTT-9779 (G7V) and WASP-121 (F6V) and de-trended the light curves by fitting the transits, eclipses, and planetary phase curves. We computed power spectra from the de-trended light curves and fit them with a Harvey granulation profile. We first analyzed the broadband light curves to measure and fix the granulation timescale and then repeated the power-spectrum analysis in individual wavelength channels to measure the chromatic dependence of the granulation amplitude. For LTT-9779, we measure a broadband granulation amplitude of σ$=53.8^{+4.1}_{-4.0}$ppm at a timescale of τ$=4.8^{+1.5}_{-1.3}$min. For WASP-121, we measure σ$=59.3\pm4.3$ppm and τ$=6.3^{+2.1}_{-1.8}$min. We also measure peak oscillation frequencies of ν$=3382^{+166}_{-191}μ$Hz and $1649^{+55}_{-69}μ$Hz in the bandpass-integrated power spectra of LTT-9779 and WASP-121, respectively. In the spectroscopic fits, we find $σ$ decreases with wavelength. Our results demonstrate a new observational window on short-timescale stellar variability and provides a way to characterize chromatic stellar noise in transit light curves.

items.title: Hidden urban exposure to energy-price shocks: spreading burdens and shifting hotspots
items.abstract: Cities need to anticipate where energy-price shocks could intensify hardship beyond established hotspots. How income distributions and fuel-price balances jointly shape this hidden exposure remains unclear. Here we address this gap by stress-testing nearly one million properties in six English local authorities, combining required-energy costs for existing housing with modelled local income distributions. Under gas-led crisis prices, 41% of neighbourhoods in the highest local exposure quarter lie outside the highest official fuel-poverty quarter. Electricity-led stress changes this hidden geography: when electricity unit prices alone triple from 2021, comparable to the unmitigated late-2022 cap increase, 38% of the resulting hidden-exposure group are absent from the crisis-based group. Entering neighbourhoods have newer, more efficient housing, more flats and greater electricity dependence than retained areas. Crisis preparedness should extend household protection beyond current hardship hotspots, using fuel-specific stress tests to anticipate support needs as fuel prices and heating systems change.

items.title: Numerical estimation of the capture ability of Neptunian mean motion resonances II. Influence of eccentricity and inclination
items.abstract: Evaluating the ability of Neptunian mean-motion resonances (MMRs) to capture small bodies is an important step in reconstructing the evolutionary history of the early Solar System. Building on a previous planar model, this study extends the investigation of MMR capture during Neptune's migration to the three-dimensional case, systematically analyzing the effects of the small objects' eccentricity, e, and inclination, i. Through numerical simulations with different migration rates, we obtain the distribution of capture probabilities for 12 MMRs on the e-i plane. The results show that increasing i narrows the ``inevitable capture zone'' (strong MMRs and/or slow migration) and raises the lower e threshold for capture (weak MMRs and/or fast migration), while it may also expand the upper e limit for capture. When the resonance order reaches three, the e-i plane further differentiates into several regions, which are closely related to the types of resonant angles. The emerging i-dominated region, along with its inevitable capture zone, makes third-order MMRs the most likely to benefit from higher inclination, as well as the most likely to host mixed-type resonators. Finally, using a hypothetical planetesimal distribution, we calculated the capture probability and efficiency for each MMR, finding that a cold disk favors strong MMRs, whereas a hot disk reduces differences among MMRs and across migration rates. In the future, a better determination of the population associated with different MMRs and different types of objects will help us understand the dynamical excitation state of the primordial disk in the early Solar System.

items.title: Long-term Age- and Region-Specific Changes in Psychiatric Service Utilization Following Japan's First COVID-19 State of Emergency.
items.abstract: To evaluate nationwide long-term changes in psychiatric service utilization across age groups following Japan's first COVID-19 state of emergency and to compare these changes across regions with different states of emergency intensities. This population-based interrupted time-series study used publicly available aggregated data derived from the National Database of Health Insurance Claims from April 2013 to April 2024, covering nearly all psychiatric patients in Japan. Segmented regression was used to estimate changes after the first state of emergency (April-May 2020). Outcomes were mean daily numbers of psychiatric outpatient visits and inpatient care per 100,000 population. Prefectures were categorized as high-, middle-, and low-intensity regions by the cumulative duration of subsequent declarations. Slope changes in psychiatric outpatient visits varied substantially by age and region. Pre-existing upward trends accelerated after the state of emergency among patients aged 15-39 and 60-69 years, with greater acceleration in high-intensity regions than in middle- or low-intensity regions. The largest change was observed among patients aged 20-24 years in high-intensity regions (0.54 [95% CI, 0.46-0.63]), compared with middle-intensity (0.34 [95% CI, 0.27-0.41]) and low-intensity regions (0.42 [95% CI, 0.34-0.50]). In contrast, psychiatric inpatient care generally declined across most age groups and regions. Following the first state of emergency, psychiatric outpatient visits increased with marked heterogeneity by age group and region, with more pronounced acceleration in high-intensity regions. These findings underscore the value of age- and region-specific monitoring of psychiatric service utilization during future public health crises.

items.title: Intratumoral and Peritumoral Functional Connectivity Reveals Network-Level Signatures of Glioma.
items.abstract: Gliomas are recognized as network-level diseases that remodel functional connectivity across the brain. Using resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) data from 306 patients with pathologically confirmed glioma at two hospitals, we delineated individualized intra- and peritumoral functional networks to quantify tumor-related alterations. Two novel indices-the ratio of intratumoral functional regions (RIFR) and ratio of peritumoral tumor-related regions (RPTR)-were proposed to describe network remodeling. Both indices were related to pathological, structural, functional, cognitive, language, and survival measures. Lower RIFR indicated diminished intratumoral connectivity and worse prognosis, while higher values reflected preserved network integration and longer survival. Models incorporating network features yielded areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.90 in training and 0.86-0.88 in external validation. Supporting analyses suggested that intratumoral functional regions are associated with distinct molecular and cellular characteristics. These findings suggest that intra- and peritumoral networks reflect biologically and functionally distinct tumor subregions and are associated with network-level alterations, brain function, and patient outcome. Interpretation is limited by the hemodynamic basis of rs-fMRI, incomplete data, and limited intraoperative validation. These findings identify individualized intra- and peritumoral connectivity measures as candidate markers of glioma-associated network remodeling and prognosis that require prospective, multimodal validation.

items.title: Channelrhodopsin ion selectivity determines mechanisms and efficacy of optogenetic defibrillation in human atria and ventricles.
items.abstract: Cardiac re-entrant arrhythmias are a major cause of sudden cardiac death. Optogenetic defibrillation has emerged as a promising anti-arrhythmic strategy based on photoactivation of channelrhodopsins, yet the efficacy and potential adverse consequences of activating different classes of light-gated ion channels have not been systematically evaluated. Previous studies assessed either cation (e.g. ChR2) or anion (e.g. GtACR1) non-selective channels, both of which depolarize resting cardiomyocytes. Recently identified light-gated K+ channels (e.g. WiChR) suppress cardiomyocyte activity while maintaining the membrane potential near its resting state, but their defibrillation potential remains unexplored. We used computational simulations to compare ChR2, GtACR1 and WiChR. Single-cell simulations showed that ChR2 and GtACR1 markedly increased diastolic intracellular Ca2+ (by 42.6% and 52.6%, respectively), whereas WiChR induced only minimal changes (by 4.0%), suggesting lower pro-arrhythmogenic risk. WiChR, however, slightly increased intracellular Na+ (by 15.1% vs. 0.1% and 3.4% for ChR2 and GtACR1), consistent with the residual Na+ permeability of currently available K+-conducting channelrhodopsins. Simulations in human ventricles and atria showed that GtACR1 most effectively terminated re-entrant arrhythmias at low light intensities, whereas WiChR achieved comparable efficacy at ≥5 mW/mm2. Complementary tissue-scale simulations revealed that defibrillation occurs through depolarization within the excitable gap followed by fast Na+ channel inactivation (ChR2 and partly GtACR1), or through reduced membrane resistance at sufficiently high light intensities (large-conductance channels GtACR1 and WiChR). Overall, we demonstrate that channelrhodopsin ion selectivity is a key determinant of both optogenetic defibrillation efficacy and its underlying mechanisms. TRANSLATIONAL PERSPECTIVE: Re-entrant arrhythmias are a leading cause of sudden cardiac death. Standard therapies, including the activation of implantable cardioverter-defibrillators, carry burdens such as pain and myocardial injury. Optogenetic defibrillation has been suggested as a potentially gentler alternative, replacing high-voltage electrical shocks by photoactivation of light-gated ion channels expressed in cardiac cells. Determining which light-gated ion channel optimally balances efficacy and adverse effects on cardiac electrophysiology is critical for clinical translation. We addressed this question using computational simulations and validation experiments in zebrafish hearts. We identify ion selectivity as a key determinant of both the success rate for arrhythmia termination and the underlying mechanisms: non-selective cation- and anion-conducting channels terminate re-entry efficiently while promoting intracellular Ca2+ accumulation, a plausible substrate for pro-arrhythmic side effects that could undermine therapeutic safety. K+-conducting channels largely avoid this pro-arrhythmic risk by holding cardiomyocytes near their resting potential, albeit at the cost of requiring transmural illumination, while also causing mild Na+ accumulation attributable to residual Na+ permeability. Together, these trade-offs define clear clinical implications: K+-conducting channels may provide the safest option for optogenetic defibrillation, particularly once variants with further enhanced K+ selectivity and red-shifted activation spectra for improved operation within blood-perfused myocardium become available. KEY POINTS: We use computational simulations to compare cation non-selective (ChR2), anion non-selective (GtACR1) and K+-selective (WiChR) channelrhodopsins for optogenetic termination of re-entrant arrhythmia. Single-cardiomyocyte simulations suggest that ChR2 and GtACR1 activation can cause progressive accumulation of intracellular Ca2+, which is minimized when using WiChR. Intracellular microelectrode recordings from hearts of transgenic adult zebrafish validate the simulated voltage dynamics seen with ChR2, GtACR1 or WiChR activation. Simulations of human left ventricles and atria indicate that GtACR1 is most effective in terminating re-entrant arrhythmia at low light intensities, whereas WiChR becomes similarly effective at higher intensities. Tissue-scale simulations indicate distinct defibrillation mechanisms: excitable gap extinction by de novo action potential initiation followed by inactivation of fast Na+ channels for depolarizing channelrhodopsins (ChR2, GtACR1), and reduction in membrane resistance for the large-conductance channels (GtACR1, WiChR), effectively clamping the membrane potential at each channel's reversal potential at high light levels.

items.title: A microglial basis for fragile X syndrome via impairment of FMRP-regulated lysosomal function.
items.abstract: Silencing of the FMRP-encoding FMR1 gene results in fragile X syndrome (FXS), the most common inheritable intellectual disability and autism. FMRP regulates various neuronal functions but clinical trials targeting neurons have failed, suggesting unrecognized disease mechanisms. We find that mice with selective Fmr1 deletion in microglia exhibit audiogenic seizures (AGS) and parvalbumin (PV) neuron loss, recapitulating two key phenotypes observed in FXS (Fmr1-/y) mice. By combining snRNA-Seq and RNA immunoprecipitation, we identify several lysosomal mRNAs as FMRP binding targets. FMRP promotes lysosomal protein expression and its deficiency disrupts lysosomal function in microglia. Notably, FMRP depletion reduces Grn-encoded secretory progranulin and increases PV neuron apoptosis in immature brains. PV neuron density is decreased similarly in Grn+/-, Fmr1-/y, and Grn+/-;Fmr1-/y mice, and progranulin overexpression rescues AGS and PV neuron loss in Fmr1-/y mice. Thus, our study identifies microglia and progranulin as critical regulators of FXS pathogenesis and potential targets for FXS therapy.

items.title: CD4+ T Cell Activation and Peripheral Immune Cell Influx into the Brain Following Wildfire Smoke Exposure is Modulated by a Saturated Fat Diet.
items.abstract: Over the past 40 years, wildfires across the United States have steadily increased, in terms of acreage burned. Smoke from wildfires can exacerbate several cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, with new studies highlighting potential sustained neurological outcomes. The purpose of this study was to delineate the role of peripheral immune populations in woodsmoke-induced neuroinflammation, the timeline of this response, and the impact of diet on each of these factors. Based on previous research on other pollutants and diet introduction, we included a highly saturated fatty acid (coconut oil) to represent the effects of a diet intervention that may modulate the severity and time course of peripheral immune infiltration. 8-week-old female C57BL/6 mice were exposed to either a sham filtered air or a woodsmoke exposure of a 0.5mg/m3 concentration every other day for 14 days, 4hr/day. Three time points were analyzed: 1-, 14-, and 28-days post exposure to woodsmoke to determine neuroinflammation at its peak and when it begins to resolve. At each time point, brains were queried by high dimensional flow cytometry analysis. Markers for peripheral immune infiltration included T cells (CD3, CD4), lymphocyte trafficking (LFA-1), resident immune cells (CD11b, ACSA-2) and other inflammation-dependent markers. Endothelial cell populations (CD31) and relevant adhesion molecules (VCAM-1, ICAM-1) were also analyzed. Results demonstrate a time and diet-dependent influx of CD4 T cells (Cd11b-, CD3+, CD4+, RORγ-, FOXP3-, CD44+), potentially to resolve neuroinflammation from woodsmoke inhalation. We also see a pattern of inflammation across several trafficking and adhesion markers, including LFA-1, VCAM-1 and ICAM-1, that peaks at 1 day after the last exposure (14 days after the initial insult). Conferred with these results are metabolomic changes in the brain including upregulated taurine and glycerolipid metabolism that is mainly tied to increased susceptibility to inflammatory phenotypes in the brain. Here, we demonstrate that woodsmoke inhalation can initiate the recruitment of peripheral immune populations and activation of endothelial cell markers within the brain. The presence of these cells implicates a larger, more persistent impact on the central nervous system following woodsmoke exposure.

items.title: Precise modeling of task-related sensorimotor activation based on simultaneous surface electromyography.
items.abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate the relationship between motor control of ankle movements and actual motor performance using simultaneous functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and surface electromyography (EMG) in healthy individuals. Twenty participants performed dorsi-/plantarflexion of the ankle (Ankle) and gait imagery in a block design during fMRI. First-level models consisting of task regressors included either orthogonalized accelerometry (Acc) from the foot, EMG from the tibialis anterior, EMG with Acc, EMG split across conditions, or none. Each model was additionally evaluated either by default with or without a temporal derivative (TD) of the ankle movement task regressor. Voxel-wise and post-hoc region-of-interest (ROI) analyses revealed that both Acc and EMG explained fMRI signal in the primary sensorimotor cortices, while EMG was additionally associated with activation in the cerebellar vermis and the secondary somatosensory cortex. The two latter findings were, however, neither reproduced when separating the signal fluctuations during rest and gait imagery nor reflected in pairwise comparisons. Leaving out the TD reduced each model's performance by increasing unexplained variance, but resulted in more signal being explained by the EMG or Acc in the cerebellum, reflecting that it preferentially exhibited brief signal changes during transitions between conditions. Taken together, both EMG and Acc enabled capturing specific brain activity related to the movement variability; however, including the TD may significantly affect the ability to detect EMG- or Acc-related signal in regions with transient fMRI responses sensitive to changes in movement context, such as the cerebellum.

items.title: Interplay of action-based prediction and top-down attention: EEG evidence for joint modulation of late perceptual processing.
items.abstract: Voluntary action shapes our perception through sensory predictions of its consequences. These predictions are thought to inhibit perceptual processing of predicted outcomes, leading to sensory attenuation. However, some studies have reported findings that contrast with this effect, suggesting that the influence of predictions may reflect, or interact with, attentional processes. Here, we investigated the interplay of action-based prediction and top-down attention on early and late perceptual processing, with prediction and attention referring to the likelihood of a sensory event and its behavioral relevance, respectively. Electroencephalography (EEG) was recorded while participants viewed two sequential gratings. The orientation of the first was either predicted and self-generated or unpredicted and externally generated. Participants judged the tilt direction of the second grating relative to the first but responded only when the grating appeared in a task-relevant color. EEG analyses revealed no modulation of early visual potentials (N1a), but modulations at later processing stages. Specifically, the P3b exhibited reduced amplitude for predicted compared to unpredicted stimuli, but only when they were task-relevant, whereas task-relevance enhanced the P3b only for unpredicted stimuli. Interestingly, multivariate pattern analysis showed significant temporal clusters for decoding the grating's orientation exclusively for predicted and task-relevant stimuli, although decoding performance did not significantly differ between conditions. Furthermore, predicted and task-relevant stimuli elicited faster behavioral responses, with prediction-related P3b latency differences correlating with reaction-time differences. Overall, converging findings from the P3b, multivariate, time-frequency and behavioral analyses provide suggestive evidence that top-down attention and action-based prediction may jointly facilitate late perceptual and decision-related processing.

items.title: Impaired causal reasoning in methamphetamine use disorder under dynamic uncertainty.
items.abstract: Preventing repeated relapse remains a central challenge in drug prevention and rehabilitation. The abstinence violation effect (AVE) highlights the importance of attribution in relapse, suggesting that when individuals misinterpret a transient lapse triggered by external circumstances as a personal failure of self-control, they may become more vulnerable to further relapse. However, the behavioral signatures and computational mechanisms of attributional reasoning under uncertainty in addiction remain poorly understood. We recruited 26 individuals with Methamphetamine Use Disorder (MUD) and 40 demographically matched healthy controls to perform an environment reasoning task (ERT), in which motion coherence manipulated confidence in perceptual decisions, allowing us to test whether negative feedback was attributed to internal perceptual errors or external environmental changes. Following negative feedback, individuals with MUD were less likely to use confidence-related perceptual evidence and accumulated negative feedback to update beliefs about external environment changes. Computational modeling further revealed individuals with MUD exhibited deficits in tracking and maintaining evidence for dynamic environmental changes. Importantly, the ability to maintain such evidence was significantly associated with abstinence duration. These findings provide process-level evidence relevant to the attributional component of AVE. Atypical causal reasoning under uncertainty may constitute a key cognitive mechanism underlying relapse, offering a computational account of how individuals respond to abstinence violations. This work provides a theoretical foundation for developing targeted cognitive-behavioral interventions aimed at reducing relapse risk.

items.title: Therapeutic Potential and Toxicological Trade-Offs of Nanoparticle-Enhanced Valproic Acid in Glioblastoma: Behavioral and Oxidative Insights.
items.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly aggressive brain tumor with a poor prognosis. In the current research, the therapeutic and behavioral efficacy of valproic acid (VPA) and its nanoparticles (Nano VPA) with or without temozolomide (TMZ) was investigated in the C6 glioblastoma rat model. We divided eighty-four adult male Wistar rats into seven groups (n=12/group): sham, tumor, TMZ, VPA, nano VPA, VPA + TMZ, and nano VPA + TMZ. To induce tumors, C6 cells were injected into the brains of the rats. On days 12 to 15, behavioral performance was assessed using the social interaction test, elevated plus maze, open field, rotarod, and passive avoidance. On day 18, tumor size, edema, and histopathology were examined. Oxidative stress parameters in brain tissue and serum were measured by ELISA. VPA and Nano VPA significantly inhibited tumor growth, either alone or with TMZ. All treatments except Nano VPA + TMZ improved survival compared with tumor controls. Treated groups showed enhanced anxiety regulation, sociability, learning, and memory. Motor coordination improved following VPA or Nano VPA therapy. Tumor induction reduced serum SOD, CAT, and TAC levels; treatments raised serum TAC and lowered brain MDA, but further reduced serum SOD. Our results suggest that oxidative stress modulation may contribute to the neurobehavioral and antitumor effects of both VPA and nano-VPA. While nano-VPA showed greater tumor reduction, conventional VPA was more effective in improving survival. Combining VPA with TMZ may enhance outcomes, and support further study of Nano VPA as an adjuvant therapy for GBM.

items.title: Stage- and context-dependent modulation of fear memory by oxytocin: neurobiological mechanisms and implications for PTSD.
items.abstract: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a multifactorial psychiatric condition characterized by re-experiencing, avoidance, hyperarousal, negative alterations in cognition and mood, and disturbances in social and emotional functioning. Within this broader clinical syndrome, persistent traumatic memories and excessive fear generalization represent important mechanistic and therapeutic domains. Despite substantial advances in understanding its neurobiological basis, current treatments remain suboptimal, with limited efficacy and high dropout rates. The neuropeptide oxytocin (OXT), a key modulator of social behavior, stress regulation, and memory, has been investigated as a potential therapeutic target. Accumulating evidence indicates that severe trauma profoundly disrupts endogenous OXTergic signaling, whereas pharmacological studies suggest that exogenous OXT can modulate fear-memory processing through region-, dose-, route-, and context-dependent mechanisms. Evidence from fear-conditioning indicates that across acquisition, consolidation, retrieval, reconsolidation, and extinction, the direction of OXT's effects is heterogeneous rather than uniformly anxiolytic and pro-extinction. OXT may influence threat discrimination, fear expression, memory updating, and extinction by modulating specific neural circuits and neurochemical pathways. However, most preclinical models capture selected dimensions of PTSD rather than the full clinical disorder. Human studies further indicate that intranasal OXT can modulate neural, physiological, and social-cognitive processes relevant to PTSD, although evidence for consistent clinical efficacy remains limited and heterogeneous. This review synthesizes current findings on OXT and its synthetic analogs within a stage- and context-dependent framework to better investigate their heterogeneous effects and assess their potential relevance and translational limitations in PTSD.

items.title: Brain folding as a Fourier series yields a developmental clock.
items.abstract: The human fetal cortex begins as a smooth spheroid and progressively folds into a stereotypical sulcal pattern. I show that the spherical-harmonic expansion - the closed-surface generalisation of Fourier's series - reproduces this developmental sequence in reverse on the group-average atlas: truncating the fully formed cortex at low maximum harmonic degree L_max recovers a younger fetal brain; progressively higher L_max recovers the primary, secondary and tertiary folds in the order in which they emerge. From this I derive a closed-form 23-dimensional log-fractional spectral descriptor. On atlas templates (17 Harvard CRL + 16 dHCP weekly templates) it predicts gestational age at MAE 0.13 and 0.38 wk across cohorts after a single supervised linear alignment, and 1.07 and 1.51 wk without. On 28 Yale-Wayne State longitudinal pairs it advances predicted GA in every subject, without cohort matching. On 80 FeTA scans (31 neurotypical, 49 pathological) off-trajectory distance discriminates pathology at AUC 0.80, and unsupervised clustering yields three internally stable, biometrically concordant subgroups - an exploratory finding requiring external validation. Individual-scan gestational-age accuracy is not the descriptor's competitive use (MAE 2.25 wk on FeTA-NT); its individual-scan value is the shape of the residual around the normative trajectory. The framework separates two spatial-scale regimes of folding onto distinguishable spectral bands and is complementary to existing measures of fetal cortical maturation.

items.title: Transdiagnostic Efficacy, Durability, and Optimal Parameters of rTMS for Cognitive Rehabilitation: A Comprehensive Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) is a promising non-invasive neuromodulation technique for cognitive rehabilitation. We evaluated the cognitive effects of rTMS on neurological and psychiatric diseases to determine moderators of efficacy. A meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs) comparing real versus sham rTMS to July 2025 was performed. Objective cognition reported as primary or secondary outcomes were extracted and Hedges' g effect sizes computed. Univariate and multivariate three-level meta-analyses were performed to estimate pooled effect sizes and assess moderator influence. 748 measures from 137 studies (5,972 participants) were extracted. Real rTMS produced a significant cognitive enhancement (g=0.28, p 0.20, I2=35.8). Neurodegenerative (g=0.35) and focal (g=0.44) conditions demonstrated stronger effects than psychiatric conditions (g=0.20). Although stimulation target was not a significant moderator overall, the Inferior Frontal Gyrus showed the largest effect (g=0.45), with significant effects also at the left and right DLPFC and left parietal cortex (g=0.29-0.45), all nodes of the Frontoparietal Network. 1-Hz stimulation produced a significantly larger effect (g=0.39) than the 10-Hz reference (g=0.19); 5-Hz, 20-Hz and iTBS were also significantly positive (g=0.30-0.49). In multivariate models, adding 10 rTMS sessions improved cognitive outcomes (Δg=+0.077), whereas increasing the number of pulses per session trended toward reduced efficacy. All effects were confirmed in a left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex subgroup analysis. Subjective cognition was measured in only 6% of studies. A multivariate prediction tool is introduced: https://amsali.shinyapps.io/tms_cognition_prediction/ CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis demonstrates the sustained efficacy of rTMS in enhancing cognitive function, with small-to-moderate effect sizes across diverse clinical populations and stimulation protocols. However, a significant gap remains regarding whether these objective neurocognitive gains translate into meaningful improvements in subjective cognition or functional outcomes.

items.title: Investigating fatigability and cortical activation during prolonged foot tapping in multiple sclerosis.
items.abstract: People with multiple sclerosis (pwMS) often exhibit motor fatigability and reduced foot-tapping ability. However, the coupling between performance and cortical activity during fast, repetitive and prolonged ankle movements remains unexplored. We aimed to investigate the neural correlates of a prolonged foot-tap task (FTT) in pwMS and healthy controls (HC). Thirty-nine pwMS (EDSS 4[3.5], 55[14] years) and 18 HC (54.5[9.75) years) performed one 1-minute FTT for each foot. Wearable sensors and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) quantified motor performance and cortical activity, respectively. fNIRS covered bilaterally frontopolar, dorsolateral prefrontal, primary motor (M1) and supplementary motor area cortices. Data were segmented into 10-second intervals and analysed via two-way ANOVA (group × time). Spearman's correlations evaluated associations between changes in cortical activity and performance (6th vs 1st segment). PwMS showed worse FTT performance with lower DLPFC activation compared to HC. On the other hand, comparable FTT performance decline over time were observed in both pwMS and HC. Cortical activity increased in SMA in HC (6 vs 2-3 intervals), but not in pwMS. In HC's, increased cortical activity across all cortical regions in the 6th interval was positive and moderately associated with less worsening in tapping performance. On the other hand, increased M1 activity was weakly associated with less foot tapping in pwMS. PwMS exhibited reduced foot-tap performance, accompanied by reduced DLPFC activation. While increased cortical activity leads to better performance in HC (i.e., a neural compensatory strategy), in pwMS increased activity was associated with worse performance (i.e., neural inefficiency).

items.title: Cannabidiol's prosexual effects in sexually active and sexually inhibited male rats.
items.abstract: Cannabidiol (CBD), a non-intoxicating, psychoactive phytocannabinoid, is being explored for its therapeutic potential on a variety of disorders. Marketed as an over-the-counter drug, it is freely available to the public. As a central nervous system acting drug, CBD has the potential to produce sexual effects, especially after its chronic use. This study characterizes the sexual effects of acute and chronic CBD oral treatment in sexually experienced male rats that were either sexually active (n = 8 per group), as a model of optimal copulatory activity, or sexually satiated (n = 8 per group), as a model of inhibited sexual behavior and decreased sexual motivation. Acute administration of CBD to sexually active males produced biphasic, dose-dependent effects on mount and intromission latencies, parameters linked to sexual motivation. In sexually satiated rats, acute treatment with CBD reversed the sexual inhibitory state at a specific dose, which also increased sexual motivation in the sexual incentive motivation test. Chronic treatment (14 days) with low and high doses of CBD did not impair male rat sexual behavior expression in the sexually active male rats. Results show that acute ingestion of CBD has prosexual effects, mainly manifested in sexual motivation, which were particularly evident in the sexually inhibited male rats. CBD chronic treatment did not produce unwanted sexual effects in the sexually active males, suggesting that it does not negatively affect male sexual behavior. The therapeutic potential of acute treatment with CBD for sexual dysfunctions involving motivational deficits should be explored.

items.title: Manifold view of spinal motor control: A paradigm in motion.
items.abstract: The neural manifold framework has transformed our understanding of cortical motor control, focusing on population dynamics that is constrained to low-dimensional structures in state space, where behaviors correspond to structured trajectories with characteristic topology. Yet the spinal cord, which houses the core circuitry responsible for rhythmic motor output such as walking, has remained largely unexplored from a manifold perspective. For decades, spinal motor function has been interpreted either through the lens of alternating flexor/extensor modules or through genetic characterization of interneurons. Both approaches struggle to amalgamate and explain how movement is flexibly generated, adapted, and stopped without losing posture. Here, we assess a new direction in spinal motor research with a focus on limbed locomotion, although we propose a general relevance, and argue that the neural manifold framework represents a complementary paradigm with the capacity to explain issues where the traditional view comes short.

items.title: Self-report measures of mindfulness for children: convergent validity, predictive validity, and impacts of social desirability bias.
items.abstract: Mindfulness-based interventions have shown promise in supporting psychological well-being in children. However, mindfulness is commonly measured using self-report questionnaires, a method that might be problematic due to its reliance on children's accurate self-perceptions of their own mindfulness and the potential influence of social desirability bias. In the current study, we examined the convergent validity, the predictive validity, and the influence of social desirability bias on three mindfulness self-report measures for children ages 9-13 years (N = 109). Results showed that children's self-reported mindfulness demonstrated good convergent validity and predictive validity, as higher levels of self-reported mindfulness were positively associated with higher levels of parent-reported executive functioning. Self-reported mindfulness also covaried with social desirability bias. However, controlling for this bias did not substantively affect the convergent validity nor the predictive validity of self-reported mindfulness. These findings suggest that children's self-reported mindfulness also captures social desirability bias, but this bias may not affect conclusions about mindfulness when assessed as a latent factor across multiple measures. Future work measuring children's mindfulness with self-reports should account for social desirability bias when possible, as well as explore objective methods of assessing mindfulness in children.
